docs.title: Woodglue
docs.text:
Self-documenting opinionated async server that hosts logic and data.

Woodglue is a JSON-RPC 2.0 server built on Tornado and lythonic that automatically generates LLM-friendly documentation from your Python functions and Pydantic models, signs people in, and hosts the UIs built on top of it.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  woodglue                                                │
│  HTTP server · JSON-RPC · Docs                           │
│  Users · Roles · Grants · Sign-in (OIDC, GitHub, proxy)  │
│  Console · project UIs (static, Streamlit)               │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  lythonic                                                │
│  Namespaces · DAGs · Caching · Triggers                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        ▲ optional: Caddy in front for TLS and static files

Woodglue is the HTTP layer; lythonic provides the core runtime (namespaces, DAG orchestration, caching, and scheduled triggers). The design decisions behind authentication and UI hosting are recorded in the ADRs under docs/adr/, and the vocabulary (User, Role, Grant, Session, Personal Access Token, Delegated Token, UI) in GLOSSARY.md.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• JSON-RPC 2.0 with multi-namespace routing — register Python functions, call them over HTTP with dot-prefixed namespace routing
  • Auto-generated docs — llms.txt index, per-method markdown, OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec, each showing only what the caller may use
  • Users, Roles, and Grants — per-namespace authorization; Personal Access Tokens that can be narrowed and expire (how-to)
  • Sign-in — Google, Entra ID, Okta, Auth0, or any OpenID Connect provider; GitHub; or a trusted proxy such as Cloudflare Access, Google IAP, or oauth2-proxy (how-to)
  • The Console — browser-based API browsing, runs and triggers, DAG visualization, and your own tokens
  • Project UIs — host your own single-page app (how-to) or Streamlit app (how-to) next to the Console, signed in as the same User
  • Run attribution — runs and trigger changes record which User caused them
  • wgl login — get a token for a remote server through the browser
  • Optional Caddy edge — wgl caddy config prints a Caddyfile (how-to)
  • Typed async client — auto-resolved return types via x-global-ref
  • YAML-driven namespace configuration — declarative setup with per-method tags and explicit gref/file/entries fields
  • DAG orchestration with scheduled triggers — workflow execution and scheduling via lythonic
  • System namespace — the server's own management API is a regular namespace (dogfooding)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# hello_api.py
from lythonic.compose.namespace import Namespace
from pydantic import BaseModel

class HelloIn(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int

class HelloOut(BaseModel):
    eman: str
    ega: int

def pydantic_hello(input: HelloIn) -> HelloOut:
    return HelloOut(eman=input.name[::-1], ega=-input.age)

ns = Namespace()
ns.register(pydantic_hello, nsref="pydantic_hello", tags=["api"])

Configure in data/woodglue.yaml:

namespaces:
  hello:
    gref: "hello_api:ns"

Run the server and get the admin token:

wgl start
wgl token          # rotate it with: wgl token --new

Open http://127.0.0.1:5321/ and sign in with the token. See Getting Started for calling the API, and the how-to guides for Users, sign-in, and UIs.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
• POST /rpc — JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
  • GET /docs/llms.txt — method index
  • GET /docs/methods/{name}.md — per-method documentation
  • GET /docs/openapi.json — OpenAPI spec
  • GET /console/ — the Console, the built-in browser UI
  • GET /ui/{name}/ — project UIs
  • GET /auth/login — browser sign-in; POST /auth/logout signs out
  • GET /auth/start/{provider}, /auth/callback/{provider} — Identity Provider sign-in
  • GET /auth/cli — approval page for wgl login
  • GET /auth/verify — access check for a reverse proxy's forward_auth

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install woodglue

Or with uv:

uv add woodglue

docs.title: Create a Namespace
docs.text:
Define your methods and register them with api tags:

# myapp/api.py
from lythonic.compose.namespace import Namespace
from pydantic import BaseModel

class GreetIn(BaseModel):
    name: str

class GreetOut(BaseModel):
    message: str

def greet(input: GreetIn) -> GreetOut:
    """Greet someone by name."""
    return GreetOut(message=f"Hello, {input.name}!")

ns = Namespace()
ns.register(greet, nsref="greet", tags=["api"])

docs.title: Configure the Server
docs.text:
Create data/woodglue.yaml, pointing at the namespace object:

namespaces:
  myapp:
    gref: "myapp.api:ns"

A namespace can also be declared in its own YAML file (myapp: {file: myapp_ns.yaml}) or inline (myapp: {entries: [...]}); see woodglue.config.NamespaceEntry.

docs.title: Start the Server
docs.text: wgl start

docs.title: Get the Auth Token
docs.text:
Auth is enabled by default (auth.enabled in woodglue.yaml). The server keeps Users, Role assignments, and tokens in data/auth.db. On first start it creates a token for the built-in admin User, which holds every Grant. wgl start never prints it. To see or rotate it:

wgl token          # print the admin token
wgl token --new    # replace it; the running server picks it up immediately

docs.title: Sign In to the Console
docs.text: Open http://127.0.0.1:5321/. It sends you to the login page; paste the admin token. The Console shows the namespaces, runs, and triggers you may see, and a Tokens page for your own Personal Access Tokens. To let people sign in with their own accounts, configure an Identity Provider: see Identity Providers.

docs.title: Give Others Access
docs.text:
Define Roles and give them to Users. For a script, create a Service User and issue it a Personal Access Token:

auth:
  roles:
    reporter: ["call myapp", "read myapp"]

wgl user add ci
wgl user assign ci reporter
wgl user issue ci nightly --days=90       # prints the secret once

See Control who can do what for Grants, Roles, and tokens.

For a remote server, sign in through the browser instead; the token is stored for that server and used by WoodglueClient:

wgl login --server=https://wg.example.com
wgl logout --server=https://wg.example.com    # revoke it

docs.title: Call via JSON-RPC
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5321/rpc \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(wgl token)" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"myapp.greet","params":{"input":{"name":"World"}},"id":1}'

docs.title: Use the Async Client
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from woodglue.client import WoodglueClient

client = WoodglueClient("http://127.0.0.1:5321", data_dir=Path("data"))
await client.load_spec(strict=True)
result = await client.call("myapp.greet", input={"name": "World"})
# result is GreetOut(message="Hello, World!")

docs.text:

  • Sign in with Google, GitHub, Entra ID, Okta, or Auth0

docs.title: Local Users, with woodglue as its own OIDC client and optional trusted proxy
docs.text:
woodglue keeps its own User records and links each one to Identity Providers, instead of treating whatever an outside login asserts as the identity. Personal Access Tokens, Role assignments, and revocation need an owner that outlives any single login, and one person may sign in through more than one provider.

woodglue runs the login flow itself as a generic OIDC client, which covers Google, Entra ID, Auth0, and Okta; GitHub, which is plain OAuth2, gets a small adapter. A trusted-proxy mode also accepts identity asserted by a reverse proxy in front of woodglue. Both paths end in the same local User, so authorization does not depend on how someone logged in.

docs.title: Considered Options
docs.text: • Delegate all login to a reverse proxy (oauth2-proxy, Cloudflare Access) and keep no local Users. Rejected: the standalone Tornado setup would have no login, and tokens for the CLI and scripts would have no owner.

docs.title: Opaque, database-checked tokens
docs.text:
Sessions, Personal Access Tokens, and Delegated Tokens are random opaque strings that are looked up in auth.db on every request. Revocation and Role changes take effect immediately, which a single server gets for the cost of one SQLite lookup.

The unused Ed25519 signed-grant model in woodglue.crypto is removed. Signed tokens only pay off when many servers must verify tokens without a shared store, and they would need a denylist to support revocation.

This assumes a single woodglue server. Several servers sharing one auth.db is not supported.

docs.title: UIs are hosted on the same origin and use an HttpOnly Session cookie
docs.text:
Project UIs are served by the same woodglue origin as the API, under /ui/<name>/, and the Console moves to /console/. Browsers authenticate with a server-set HttpOnly Session cookie, so no page script, including a project UI, can read a credential. Because the cookie is sent automatically, /rpc accepts only application/json requests and checks Origin as CSRF protection.

Before a request reaches a process-backed UI, such as Streamlit, the proxy strips the Session cookie and injects the User's identity and a Delegated Token tied to the Session. A buggy or hostile UI process therefore never holds a credential that outlives the Session.

docs.title: Considered Options
docs.text: • UIs on separate origins with CORS, each running its own OAuth flow and holding a bearer token. Deferred: possible later for CDN-hosted UIs, not the default.

docs.title: Caddy is an optional edge; woodglue owns auth
docs.text:
woodglue runs complete without Caddy. Tornado serves static UIs and also proxies process-backed UIs such as Streamlit, including their websockets. When Caddy is used, it adds TLS, multiple domains, and serving static UI files at the edge, and it asks woodglue who each request belongs to through forward_auth. Users, Sessions, and Grants never live in Caddy.

Process-backed UIs stay behind woodglue's own proxy even with Caddy in front: woodglue picks their ports when it starts them, and stripping the Session cookie, issuing Delegated Tokens, and closing websockets at sign-out belong in one place.

docs.title: Considered Options
docs.text:
• OIDC inside Caddy through plugins such as caddy-security. Rejected: it needs a custom Caddy build, cannot enforce Grants per JSON-RPC method (the method name is inside the request body), and would duplicate the logic the standalone setup needs anyway.
  • Require Caddy for process-backed UIs and serve only static UIs from Tornado. Rejected: a laptop with a Streamlit UI would need a Caddy binary, which costs more than the Tornado proxy (prior art: jupyter-server-proxy).

docs.title: Control who can do what
docs.text: Every request runs as a User, and what a User may do is the sum of the Grants in their Roles. Reference: woodglue.access, woodglue.auth_store, and woodglue.apps.system_api.

docs.title: Grants and Roles
docs.text:
A Grant is "<action> <pattern>". The pattern is a glob over namespace names, or over ui:<name> for UIs:

Action Allows call calling the namespace's methods read seeing its runs, run inputs and outputs, and triggers trigger firing, activating, and deactivating its triggers view opening a UI: view ui:reports, view ui:console, view ui:* admin managing Users, Role assignments, and others' tokens

No action implies another: call reports does not let anyone see its runs.

Roles are named sets of Grants in woodglue.yaml. admin is built in and holds every Grant:

auth:
  roles:
    viewer: ["read *", "view ui:*"]
    operator: ["call *", "read *", "trigger *", "view ui:*"]
    reporter: ["call reports", "view ui:reports"]

A User sees only the namespaces they hold some Grant on: others are missing from system.list_namespaces, llms.txt, and openapi.json, and calling them answers -32601 Method not found. A visible namespace without the needed Grant answers -32003 Forbidden.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
• People are created when they first sign in through an Identity Provider, which can also give them Roles (default_roles, group_roles) and re-applies those at every sign-in. Emails listed in auth.admins get admin. See Identity Providers.
  • Service Users are for daemons and CI. They have no sign-in, only Personal Access Tokens.
  • admin is a built-in Service User; wgl token prints its tokens.
wgl user add ci                 # create a Service User
wgl user assign ci reporter     # give a Role (also: unassign)
wgl user list                   # Users, kinds, Roles, state
wgl user disable ci             # also revokes all its credentials (enable undoes the disable)

A <user> is a User id, email, or unique name. Admins can do the same over the API with system.list_users, create_service_user, assign_role, unassign_role, disable_user, and enable_user.

docs.title: Personal Access Tokens
docs.text:
Scripts send a token as Authorization: Bearer <token>. A token can expire, and can be narrowed to some of its User's Grants. It never exceeds them: if the User loses a Role, the token loses it too.

wgl user issue ci nightly --days=90 --grants="call reports"   # prints the secret once
wgl user tokens ci
wgl user revoke tok_1a2b3c

Signed-in people manage their own tokens on the Console's Tokens page, or with system.create_token, list_tokens, and revoke_token. For a remote server, wgl login --server=URL gets one through the browser.

A narrowed token cannot create tokens or start a browser Session, so it cannot mint anything broader than itself.

docs.title: UIs
docs.text: Opening the Console needs view ui:console, and a project UI view ui:<name>, unless the UI is public. A Process-backed UI (Streamlit, or any server woodglue proxies) calls the API as the viewer, limited to the UI's own grants. See Host a Streamlit app.

docs.title: Turning auth off
docs.text: auth.enabled: false runs every request as an anonymous User with every Grant, for local development. wgl start warns if the server then listens on anything but loopback.

docs.title: Run woodglue behind Caddy
docs.text: woodglue runs complete on its own. Put Caddy in front when you want automatic HTTPS, a real domain, or static UI files served at the edge. Caddy never decides who may do what: it asks woodglue (see docs/adr/0004). Reference: woodglue.caddy.

docs.title: Generate the Caddyfile
docs.text:
wgl --data /srv/woodglue caddy config wg.example.com > /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
sudo systemctl reload caddy

The generated site:

  • gets a certificate for wg.example.com automatically;
  • removes client-sent X-Woodglue-User and X-Woodglue-Token headers;
  • serves each Static UI's files from disk. Before each request, forward_auth asks woodglue's /auth/verify whether the viewer may open the UI, so a visitor without a Session is sent to the login page and back, and one without view on ui:<name> gets 403;
  • sends everything else to woodglue: /rpc, /docs, /auth, the Console, and Process-backed UIs such as Streamlit. woodglue runs those processes on ports it picks at start, and keeps their Session handling (cookie stripping, Delegated Tokens, closing websockets on sign-out) in one place.

Regenerate the file after adding or removing a Static UI.

docs.title: Configure woodglue for it
docs.text:
Keep woodglue on loopback so it is only reachable through Caddy, and tell it the public address so sign-in callbacks point at Caddy:

host: 127.0.0.1
port: 5321
auth:
  public_url: https://wg.example.com

docs.title: Put another app behind woodglue sign-in
docs.text:
/auth/verify works for any app Caddy proxies on the same site, since the browser sends woodglue's Session cookie only to woodglue's own host. Name the UI with ?ui= and grant view ui:<name> to the Roles that may use it. Add a block like this to the generated site, before its final handle:

    handle /grafana/* {
        forward_auth 127.0.0.1:5321 {
            uri /auth/verify?ui=grafana
            copy_headers X-Woodglue-User
        }
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
    }

The app receives X-Woodglue-User, but Caddy passes the woodglue Session cookie through to it. For an app that should never see that cookie, configure it as an upstream: UI instead and let woodglue proxy it.

docs.title: Sign in with Google, GitHub, Entra ID, Okta, or Auth0
docs.text: woodglue signs people in through any OpenID Connect provider, and through GitHub. Each person becomes a local User the first time they sign in, gets Roles from the provider's settings, and receives a browser Session. Field reference: woodglue.config.ProviderConfig.

docs.title: Register woodglue with the provider
docs.text:
Create an OAuth "web application" client at the provider and set its redirect (callback) URL to:

https://<your woodglue host>/auth/callback/<provider id>

Behind a proxy, set auth.public_url to the address browsers use, so woodglue builds the same callback URL:

auth:
  public_url: https://wg.example.com

Keep the client secret out of woodglue.yaml by referencing an environment variable as ${NAME}. wgl start refuses to start if the variable is unset.

docs.title: Configure providers
docs.text:
auth:
  roles:
    viewer: ["read *", "view ui:*"]
    operator: ["call *", "read *", "trigger *", "view ui:*"]
  admins: [you@example.com]          # get the admin Role at sign-in
  providers:
    - id: google
      kind: oidc
      label: Google
      issuer: https://accounts.google.com
      client_id: 1234.apps.googleusercontent.com
      client_secret: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}
      admit:
        email_domains: [example.com]
      default_roles: [viewer]

    - id: entra
      kind: oidc
      label: Microsoft
      issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant id>/v2.0
      client_id: ${ENTRA_CLIENT_ID}
      client_secret: ${ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET}
      trust_email: true                  # Entra sends no email_verified claim
      admit:
        email_domains: [example.com]
      default_roles: [viewer]

    - id: okta
      kind: oidc
      label: Okta
      issuer: https://example.okta.com    # or an authorization server URL
      client_id: ${OKTA_CLIENT_ID}
      client_secret: ${OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET}
      scopes: [openid, email, profile, groups]
      admit:
        groups: [woodglue-users]
      default_roles: [viewer]
      group_roles:
        woodglue-operators: [operator]

    - id: auth0
      kind: oidc
      label: Auth0
      issuer: https://example.us.auth0.com/
      client_id: ${AUTH0_CLIENT_ID}
      client_secret: ${AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET}
      admit:
        emails: [contractor@gmail.com]
      default_roles: [viewer]

    - id: github
      kind: github
      label: GitHub
      client_id: ${GITHUB_CLIENT_ID}
      client_secret: ${GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET}
      admit:
        groups: [my-org]                 # org members
      group_roles:
        my-org/platform: [operator]      # team members

docs.title: Admission
docs.text:
Every provider needs an admit rule; a person signs in if any rule matches. Rules are checked at every sign-in, so someone who leaves a group is refused from then on.

  • email_domains and emails only count an email the provider says is verified. Entra ID never says so; set trust_email: true for a single-tenant Entra client, whose addresses your organization controls.
  • groups matches the provider's groups claim (groups_claim, default groups). Okta and Entra need the groups claim enabled on the client. For GitHub, a group is an org login (my-org) or a team (my-org/platform).
  • anyone: true admits everyone the provider vouches for. For Google or GitHub that is anyone on the internet, so pair it with Roles that grant little.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: default_roles and the Roles group_roles maps to are re-applied at every sign-in: removing someone from woodglue-operators in Okta removes operator at their next sign-in. Roles given with wgl user assign are kept.

docs.title: One person, several providers
docs.text: A User found by a provider is linked to it. When someone signs in through a second provider with the same verified email, that provider is linked to the same User. A provider that does not verify the email gets a separate User, so an unverified address cannot take over an account.

docs.title: Tokens still work
docs.text: The login page always offers a Personal Access Token form, and scripts keep using Authorization: Bearer. Signed-in people create their own tokens on the Console's Tokens page.

docs.title: Behind an authenticating proxy
docs.text:
When a proxy such as Cloudflare Access, Google IAP, or oauth2-proxy already signs people in, let woodglue trust what it asserts instead. There is no login page: the first request carrying a valid assertion signs the person in, with the same admit rules and Roles as above, and starts a Session.

A signed JWT in a header is the safe choice, since woodglue checks the signature, issuer, audience, and expiry:

auth:
  providers:
    - id: cloudflare
      kind: trusted_proxy_jwt
      header: Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion
      jwks_url: https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs
      issuer: https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com
      audience: <application audience tag>
      admit: {email_domains: [example.com]}
      default_roles: [viewer]

    - id: iap
      kind: trusted_proxy_jwt
      header: x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion
      jwks_url: https://www.gstatic.com/iap/verify/public_key-jwk
      issuer: https://cloud.google.com/iap
      audience: /projects/<number>/global/backendServices/<id>
      admit: {email_domains: [example.com]}

A proxy that sends plain headers (oauth2-proxy with --set-xauthrequest, many internal gateways) can be trusted too, but only from its own addresses, since anyone reaching woodglue directly could send the same header:

    - id: oauth2-proxy
      kind: trusted_proxy_header
      header: X-Forwarded-Email
      name_header: X-Forwarded-Preferred-Username
      groups_header: X-Forwarded-Groups      # comma-separated
      trusted_sources: [127.0.0.1/32, 10.0.0.0/8]
      admit: {groups: [woodglue-users]}

Keep woodglue unreachable except through the proxy in either case.

docs.title: Host a project UI
docs.text: A woodglue server can host your own web interface next to the Console, on the same origin as /rpc. Users sign in once, and the UI calls the API with their Session cookie: it never handles a token. Reference: woodglue.config.UiEntry and woodglue.apps.uis.

docs.title: Build the app for its mount path
docs.text:
A UI named reports is served at /ui/reports/, so build it with that base. For Vite (React, Vue, Svelte, or plain JS):

// vite.config.js
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  base: "/ui/reports/",
  build: { outDir: "dist" },
});

Client-side routers need the same base, e.g. createBrowserRouter(routes, { basename: "/ui/reports" }) in React Router.

docs.title: Call the API
docs.text:
Send JSON-RPC to /rpc from the same origin. The browser attaches the Session cookie; the request must be application/json, which fetch with a JSON body already is:

let id = 0;

export async function rpc(method, params = {}) {
  const resp = await fetch("/rpc", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", method, params, id: ++id }),
  });
  const data = await resp.json();
  if (data.error?.code === -32000) {
    // The Session ended; sign in again and come back here.
    location.assign(`/auth/login?next=${encodeURIComponent(location.pathname)}`);
  }
  if (data.error) throw new Error(data.error.message);
  return data.result;
}

const me = await rpc("system.whoami");
const rows = await rpc("reports.daily_totals", { day: "2026-10-01" });

system.whoami gives the signed-in User's name, email, and Roles, for display. Authorization is still enforced by the server on every call.

docs.title: Configure the UI
docs.text:
Point woodglue.yaml at the build output (relative to the data dir):

uis:
  reports:
    path: ../frontend/dist
    label: Reports
ui:
  default: reports        # `/` lands here instead of the Console
auth:
  roles:
    analyst: ["call reports", "view ui:reports"]
  • Opening the UI needs view on ui:reports. Without a Session, a page load redirects to the login page and back.
  • spa_fallback (on by default) serves index.html for paths like /ui/reports/runs/42, so client-side routes survive a reload. Paths with a file extension still 404.
  • public: true serves the files without sign-in, e.g. for a status page. The API calls it makes still need a Caller.

The Console links to every UI the signed-in User may open (system.list_uis).

docs.title: Host a Streamlit app (or another Python web app)
docs.text: woodglue can run a Streamlit app, or any web server, and serve it at /ui/<name>/ next to the Console. People sign in to woodglue once; the app learns who is viewing and calls the woodglue API as them, with exactly their Grants. Reference: woodglue.config.UiEntry, woodglue.apps.ui_process, woodglue.apps.ui_proxy, and woodglue.ui_support.

docs.title: Streamlit
docs.text:
Install Streamlit in the same environment as woodglue, then configure the app (paths are relative to the data dir):

uis:
  dash:
    kind: streamlit
    app: dashboards/app.py
    label: Dashboards
    grants: ["call reports"]      # all the app may do, whoever views it
auth:
  roles:
    analyst: ["call reports", "view ui:dash"]

wgl start runs streamlit run on a free loopback port with --server.baseUrlPath=ui/dash, waits for /_stcore/health, and restarts the app if it exits. Set dev: true to reload the app when its files change.

In the app, ask woodglue who is viewing and call the API as them:

import asyncio

import streamlit as st

from woodglue.ui_support import current_client, current_user

me = current_user()
st.write(f"Hello, {me.name}")


async def load():
    return await current_client().call("reports.daily_totals", day="2026-10-01")


st.dataframe(asyncio.run(load()))

A complete example is in examples/streamlit/:

uv run --with streamlit wgl --data examples/streamlit start

docs.title: Any other web server
docs.text:
Give the command line instead; {port} and {base_path} are filled in. The server must listen on 127.0.0.1:{port} and serve everything under {base_path} (/ui/<name>), since woodglue forwards paths unchanged:

uis:
  board:
    command: [python, -m, myboard, --port, "{port}", --root-path, "{base_path}"]
    ready_path: /ui/board/healthz      # default: /ui/board/
    env: {BOARD_THEME: dark}

For a server you run yourself, give its address instead; woodglue only proxies to it:

uis:
  grafana:
    upstream: http://127.0.0.1:3000   # serving under /ui/grafana

docs.title: What the app receives
docs.text:
Every request and websocket woodglue forwards carries:

  • X-Woodglue-User: JSON with the viewer's id, name, email, and roles.
  • X-Woodglue-Token: a Delegated Token for the viewer's browser Session. It calls the API with the viewer's Grants, limited to the UI's grants when set, and stops working when they sign out or their Session expires.

Set grants to what the app needs. Without it, the app acts with everything the viewer may do: when an admin opens it, the app process could manage Users or fire any trigger. With it, the app is limited to the overlap of the viewer's Grants and its own, so a viewer without call reports still cannot call reports through the app.

The app calling the API does not keep the viewer's Session alive. A Session ends after 12 hours without the viewer's own requests (page loads and websocket connections through the app count), even if the app keeps polling.

woodglue removes its own Session cookie and any client-sent X-Woodglue-* header first, and keeps the app's own cookies. Websockets close when the viewer signs out. The process gets WOODGLUE_URL, the API's loopback address, in its environment.

Only trust these headers when the app is reachable through woodglue alone: keep it on loopback, as woodglue does for the processes it runs.

The Console lists each UI with its state while the process is starting or restarting; the proxy answers 503 until it is ready.

Grants, Roles, and the Caller of a request.

Authorization model: Grants, Roles, and the Caller of a request.

A Grant permits one action on the targets matching a glob pattern. Actions:

  • call: invoke methods of a namespace.
  • read: see runs, run IO, and triggers of a namespace.
  • trigger: fire, activate, and deactivate triggers of a namespace.
  • view: open a UI; its targets are ui:<name>.
  • admin: manage Users, Role assignments, and tokens. Its pattern is ignored.

No action implies another. Grants are written as "<action> <pattern>" strings in woodglue.yaml; a bare "admin" needs no pattern:

auth:
  roles:
    operator: ["call reports", "read *", "trigger reports"]
    viewer: ["read *", "view ui:*"]

The admin Role is built in and holds every Grant.

A Caller is who a request runs as. It carries one or more Grant sets and is allowed an action only if every set allows it, so a narrowed Personal Access Token never exceeds its User's current Grants. current_caller holds the Caller while a JSON-RPC call runs; it is unset for trusted in-process calls (tests, wgl run), which check then allows.

class Grant(BaseModel):
    """
    Permission to perform `action` on targets matching the glob `pattern`.

    >>> Grant.parse("call reports")
    Grant(action=<Action.call: 'call'>, pattern='reports')
    >>> str(Grant.parse("admin"))
    'admin *'
    """

    model_config: ConfigDict = ConfigDict(frozen=True)  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleVariableOverride]

    action: Action
    pattern: str = "*"

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Grant:
        parts = text.split()
        if len(parts) == 1 and parts[0] == Action.admin:
            return cls(action=Action.admin)
        if len(parts) != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Grant must be '<action> <pattern>', got {text!r}")
        try:
            action = Action(parts[0])
        except ValueError:
            valid = ", ".join(a.value for a in Action)
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown action {parts[0]!r} in grant {text!r}; use {valid}"
            ) from None
        return cls(action=action, pattern=parts[1])

    def matches(self, action: Action, target: str) -> bool:
        if action != self.action:
            return False
        return action == Action.admin or fnmatchcase(target, self.pattern)

    @override
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.action} {self.pattern}"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Caller:
    """
    Who a request runs as. `user_id` is `None` only for the anonymous Caller
    used when auth is disabled. `credential_id` and `credential_kind` name the
    token or Session that authenticated the request.
    """

    user_id: str | None
    grant_sets: tuple[tuple[Grant, ...], ...]
    credential_id: str | None = None
    credential_kind: str | None = None
    name: str = ""
    email: str | None = None
    roles: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

    def can(self, action: Action, target: str = "") -> bool:
        return all(allows(gs, action, target) for gs in self.grant_sets)

    @property
    def narrowed(self) -> bool:
        return len(self.grant_sets) > 1

    @property
    def may_issue_credentials(self) -> bool:
        """
        Whether this Caller may create tokens or Sessions. Only an unnarrowed
        Personal Access Token or a Session may: a narrowed token could mint
        one broader than itself, and a Delegated Token one that outlives its
        Session.
        """
        return (
            self.user_id is not None
            and not self.narrowed
            and self.credential_kind
            in (
                "token",
                "session",
            )
        )

    def can_see(self, namespace: str) -> bool:
        """Whether `namespace` appears in discovery for this Caller."""
        return any(self.can(a, namespace) for a in NAMESPACE_ACTIONS)

def allows(grants: Iterable[Grant], action: Action, target: str = "") -> bool:
    """
    Whether any of `grants` permits `action` on `target`.

    >>> gs = [Grant.parse("call rep*"), Grant.parse("view ui:*")]
    >>> allows(gs, Action.call, "reports"), allows(gs, Action.call, "billing")
    (True, False)
    >>> allows(gs, Action.read, "reports")
    False
    >>> allows(gs, Action.view, "ui:billing")
    True
    """
    return any(g.matches(action, target) for g in grants)

def resolve_roles(roles: dict[str, list[str]]) -> dict[str, tuple[Grant, ...]]:
    """
    Parse Role definitions from config and add the built-in `admin` Role.

    >>> r = resolve_roles({"viewer": ["read *"]})
    >>> sorted(r), [str(g) for g in r["viewer"]]
    (['admin', 'viewer'], ['read *'])
    """
    if ADMIN_ROLE in roles:
        raise ValueError(f"Role '{ADMIN_ROLE}' is built in and cannot be redefined")
    resolved = {name: tuple(Grant.parse(g) for g in grants) for name, grants in roles.items()}
    resolved[ADMIN_ROLE] = ALL_GRANTS
    return resolved

def visible(names: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Filter namespace names to those the current Caller can see."""
    caller = current_caller.get()
    if caller is None:
        return list(names)
    return [n for n in names if caller.can_see(n)]

docs.text:
Browser login, logout, and the Identity Provider round trip.

Browser login and logout: /auth/login, /auth/logout, and the Identity Provider round trip at /auth/start/<provider> and /auth/callback/<provider> (see woodglue.apps.identity_providers).

Every way in ends in a Session and the wgl_session cookie (see woodglue.apps.authn). The login page offers a button per configured Identity Provider, and always a form for a Personal Access Token, e.g. the output of wgl token. A narrowed token is refused, since the Session it would start would carry all of the User's Grants.

/auth/cli and /auth/cli/token let wgl login get a Personal Access Token for the signed-in User: the browser approves on the server's page, which hands a one-time code to the CLI's loopback address; the CLI exchanges the code, with the PKCE verifier only it knows, for the token (see woodglue.cli_login). The token itself never appears in a URL.

The login pages accept a next path to return to; anything that is not a path on this server is replaced by /, so the login page cannot be used as an open redirect.

class LoginHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """GET shows the login page; POST exchanges a token for a Session."""

    @override
    def get(self) -> None:
        self.write(_login_page(self, safe_next(self.get_argument("next", None))))

    @override
    def post(self) -> None:
        if not is_same_origin(self.request):
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(403, "Cross-site login rejected")
        next_url = safe_next(self.get_argument("next", None))
        store: AuthStore = self.application.settings["auth_store"]
        caller = store.resolve(self.get_argument("token", "").strip())
        error = None
        if caller is None or caller.user_id is None or caller.credential_kind != "token":
            error = "That token is not valid."
        elif not caller.may_issue_credentials:
            error = "That token is narrowed; sign in with an unnarrowed token."
        if error is not None:
            self.set_status(401)
            self.write(_login_page(self, next_url, error))
            return
        assert caller is not None and caller.user_id is not None
        set_session_cookie(self, store.create_session(caller.user_id))
        self.redirect(next_url)

class LogoutHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """POST ends the Session, closes its UI websockets, and returns to the login page."""

    @override
    def post(self) -> None:
        if not is_same_origin(self.request):
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(403, "Cross-site logout rejected")
        auth = authenticate(self)
        store: AuthStore = self.application.settings["auth_store"]
        if auth.session_secret is not None:
            store.end_session(auth.session_secret)
            sockets: UiSockets = self.application.settings["ui_sockets"]
            sockets.close_session(auth.session_secret)
        clear_session_cookie(self)
        self.redirect("/auth/login")

class StartSignInHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """GET `/auth/start/<provider>`: send the browser to the Identity Provider."""

    @override
    async def get(self, provider_id: str) -> None:
        client = _client(self, provider_id)
        pending = PendingSignIn(
            provider=provider_id,
            next_url=safe_next(self.get_argument("next", None)),
            redirect_uri=f"{_public_base(self)}/auth/callback/{provider_id}",
        )
        pending_sign_ins: PendingSignIns = self.application.settings["pending_sign_ins"]
        state = pending_sign_ins.add(pending)
        try:
            url = await client.authorize_url(pending, state)
        except SignInError as exc:
            logger.warning("Sign-in with %s could not start: %s", provider_id, exc)
            self.set_status(502)
            self.write(
                _login_page(self, pending.next_url, f"{client.config.display_name} is unavailable.")
            )
            return
        # Ties the callback to this browser, so nobody can complete a sign-in they did not start.
        self.set_cookie(
            LOGIN_COOKIE,
            state,
            path="/auth/",
            httponly=True,
            samesite="Lax",
            secure=public_scheme(self) == "https",
            expires_days=None,
        )
        self.redirect(url)

class SignInCallbackHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """GET `/auth/callback/<provider>`: finish a sign-in and start a Session."""

    @override
    async def get(self, provider_id: str) -> None:
        client = _client(self, provider_id)
        state = self.get_argument("state", "")
        if not state or self.get_cookie(LOGIN_COOKIE) != state:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "Sign-in state does not match this browser")
        self.clear_cookie(LOGIN_COOKIE, path="/auth/")
        pending_sign_ins: PendingSignIns = self.application.settings["pending_sign_ins"]
        pending = pending_sign_ins.pop(state)
        if pending is None or pending.provider != provider_id:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "Sign-in expired; start again")
        name = client.config.display_name
        if self.get_argument("error", None):
            self._fail(401, pending, f"{name} did not sign you in: {self.get_argument('error')}")
            return
        try:
            who = await client.complete(pending, self.get_argument("code", ""))
        except SignInError as exc:
            logger.warning("Sign-in with %s failed: %s", provider_id, exc)
            self._fail(401, pending, f"Sign-in with {name} failed.")
            return
        if not admits(client.config.admit, who):
            logger.info("Sign-in with %s refused for %s (%s)", provider_id, who.subject, who.email)
            self._fail(403, pending, f"Your {name} account is not allowed on this server.")
            return
        store: AuthStore = self.application.settings["auth_store"]
        auth_config: AuthConfig = self.application.settings["config"].auth
        try:
            user = store.sign_in_person(
                provider_id,
                who.subject,
                email=who.email,
                email_verified=who.email_verified,
                name=who.name,
                role_sources=role_sources(client.config, who, auth_config.admins),
            )
        except UserDisabled:
            self._fail(403, pending, "Your account is disabled.")
            return
        logger.info("Signed in %s (%s) with %s", user.id, user.email, provider_id)
        set_session_cookie(self, store.create_session(user.id))
        self.redirect(pending.next_url)

    def _fail(self, status: int, pending: PendingSignIn, error: str) -> None:
        self.set_status(status)
        self.write(_login_page(self, pending.next_url, error))

class CliCodes:
    """One-time codes handed to a CLI's loopback address, by code."""

    _codes: dict[str, _CliCode]

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._codes = {}

    def add(self, user_id: str, name: str, challenge: str) -> str:
        """Issue a code for an approved request, dropping expired ones."""
        cutoff = time.monotonic() - _CLI_CODE_TTL_SECONDS
        self._codes = {c: v for c, v in self._codes.items() if v.created >= cutoff}
        code = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        self._codes[code] = _CliCode(user_id, name, challenge)
        return code

    def redeem(self, code: str, verifier: str) -> _CliCode | None:
        """
        The approval behind `code` if `verifier` matches its challenge. Any
        attempt uses the code up, so a wrong verifier cannot be retried.
        """
        entry = self._codes.pop(code, None)
        if entry is None or time.monotonic() - entry.created > _CLI_CODE_TTL_SECONDS:
            return None
        if not secrets.compare_digest(pkce_challenge(verifier), entry.challenge):
            return None
        return entry

class CliAuthorizeHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """GET shows the approval page; POST issues a one-time code to the CLI's loopback address."""

    def _params(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        params = {
            k: self.get_argument(k, "") for k in ("redirect_uri", "state", "code_challenge", "name")
        }
        if not is_loopback_redirect(params["redirect_uri"]) or not params["code_challenge"]:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "redirect_uri must be a loopback address with a port")
        params["name"] = params["name"].strip() or "wgl"
        return params

    def _caller(self) -> Caller | None:
        caller = authenticate(self).caller
        if caller is None:
            self.redirect(f"/auth/login?next={quote(self.request.uri or '/', safe='')}")
        elif caller.user_id is None:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "Auth is disabled; the CLI needs no token")
        elif not caller.may_issue_credentials:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(403, "This credential cannot create tokens")
        return caller

    @override
    def get(self) -> None:
        params = self._params()
        caller = self._caller()
        if caller is None:
            return
        fields = "".join(
            f'<input type="hidden" name="{k}" value="{html.escape(v, quote=True)}">'
            for k, v in params.items()
        )
        self.write(
            _CONFIRM_PAGE.format(
                name=html.escape(params["name"]),
                user=html.escape(caller.email or caller.name),
                fields=fields,
            )
        )

    @override
    def post(self) -> None:
        if not is_same_origin(self.request):
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(403, "Cross-site authorization rejected")
        params = self._params()
        caller = self._caller()
        if caller is None:
            return
        assert caller.user_id is not None
        codes: CliCodes = self.application.settings["cli_codes"]
        code = codes.add(caller.user_id, params["name"], params["code_challenge"])
        self.redirect(
            f"{params['redirect_uri']}?{urlencode({'code': code, 'state': params['state']})}"
        )

class CliTokenHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """POST `{code, code_verifier}`: the Personal Access Token for an approved code."""

    @override
    def post(self) -> None:
        try:
            body = json.loads(self.request.body)
            code, verifier = str(body["code"]), str(body["code_verifier"])
        except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "Expected JSON with code and code_verifier") from None
        codes: CliCodes = self.application.settings["cli_codes"]
        entry = codes.redeem(code, verifier)
        if entry is None:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "Unknown, expired, or already used code")
        store: AuthStore = self.application.settings["auth_store"]
        issued = store.create_token(entry.user_id, entry.name)
        logger.info("Issued CLI token %s to %s", issued.id, entry.user_id)
        self.write({"token": issued.secret, "id": issued.id})

def safe_next(target: str | None) -> str:
    """
    A local path to redirect to after login, or `/`.

    >>> safe_next("/console/#runs"), safe_next("//evil.example"), safe_next("https://x/")
    ('/console/#runs', '/', '/')
    >>> safe_next("/\\\\evil.example"), safe_next(None)
    ('/', '/')
    """
    if not target or not target.startswith("/") or target[1:2] in ("/", "\\"):
        return "/"
    return target

def is_loopback_redirect(uri: str) -> bool:
    """
    Whether `uri` points at a CLI listening on this computer.

    >>> is_loopback_redirect("http://127.0.0.1:53111/cb"), is_loopback_redirect("http://localhost:9/")
    (True, True)
    >>> is_loopback_redirect("http://127.0.0.1/cb"), is_loopback_redirect("https://evil.example:9/")
    (False, False)
    """
    parts = urlsplit(uri)
    return (
        parts.scheme == "http"
        and parts.hostname in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")
        and parts.port is not None
    )

Request authentication: bearer tokens and the Session cookie.

Request authentication shared by the woodglue HTTP handlers.

authenticate turns a request into a woodglue.access.Caller, reading the application settings auth_enabled and auth_store. An app with auth disabled serves every request as the anonymous Caller.

A request authenticates in one of these ways, tried in order:

  • Authorization: Bearer <token>, for the CLI, scripts, and LLM tooling.
  • An identity asserted by a trusted reverse proxy (see woodglue.apps.identity_providers.TrustedProxy). The first valid assertion signs the person in and sets a Session cookie; later requests reuse that Session while the proxy keeps asserting the same person.
  • The wgl_session cookie, set by /auth/login for browsers. It is HttpOnly, so no page script (including a project UI) can read it (see docs/adr/0003).

The last two arrive automatically with any browser request, so both count as cookie authentication, and state-changing handlers must call is_same_origin for them.

Tokens in query strings are not accepted, since URLs end up in logs, browser history, and Referer headers.

def authenticate(handler: tornado.web.RequestHandler) -> Authentication:
    """Who sent this request and how, trying the ways above in order."""
    settings = handler.application.settings
    if not settings.get("auth_enabled", False):
        return Authentication(ANONYMOUS, AuthVia.anonymous)
    store: AuthStore | None = settings.get("auth_store")
    if store is None:
        return Authentication(None, AuthVia.anonymous)
    token = bearer_token(handler.request)
    if token:
        return Authentication(store.resolve(token), AuthVia.bearer)
    proxied = _proxy_authentication(handler, store)
    if proxied is not None:
        return proxied
    secret = handler.get_cookie(SESSION_COOKIE)
    if secret:
        return Authentication(store.resolve(secret), AuthVia.cookie, secret)
    return Authentication(None, AuthVia.anonymous)

def is_same_origin(request: tornado.httputil.HTTPServerRequest) -> bool:
    """
    Whether a browser request comes from this server's own pages. Uses `Origin`,
    falling back to `Referer`; a request with neither is not a browser
    cross-site request and passes.
    """
    source = request.headers.get("Origin") or request.headers.get("Referer")
    if source is None:
        return True
    return urlsplit(source).netloc == request.host

def public_scheme(handler: tornado.web.RequestHandler) -> str:
    """
    The scheme browsers use to reach this server: that of `auth.public_url`
    when set, since a proxy terminating TLS forwards plain HTTP, else the
    request's own.
    """
    config = handler.application.settings.get("config")
    public_url = config.auth.public_url if config is not None else None
    return urlsplit(public_url).scheme if public_url else handler.request.protocol

docs.title: woodglue.apps.identity_providers
docs.text:
OpenID Connect and GitHub sign-in.

Signing in through Identity Providers: OpenID Connect, GitHub, and trusted reverse proxies.

woodglue is its own OAuth client (see docs/adr/0001). A sign-in is the authorization code flow with PKCE:

  • /auth/start/<provider> records a pending sign-in (state, nonce, PKCE verifier, and where to return), binds it to the browser with a short-lived wgl_login cookie, and redirects to the provider.
  • /auth/callback/<provider> checks that the returned state matches the cookie, exchanges the code, and turns the provider's answer into an ExternalIdentity. For OIDC that is the validated id_token (issuer, audience, expiry, nonce, signature against the provider's JWKS); for GitHub it is the user, verified primary email, orgs, and teams from the API.
  • The person is then checked against the provider's admit rules, signed in as a local User (AuthStore.sign_in_person), and given a Session.

Admission and claim-to-Role mapping are re-evaluated at every sign-in.

A trusted proxy (JwtProxy, HeaderProxy) has no round trip: it asserts the identity on every request, and woodglue.apps.authn turns the first valid assertion into a Session.

Pending sign-ins live in memory for ten minutes, so a restart in the middle of one only means signing in again.

class PendingSignIns:
    """In-memory pending sign-ins keyed by OAuth `state`."""

    _items: dict[str, PendingSignIn]

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items = {}

    def add(self, pending: PendingSignIn) -> str:
        self._expire()
        state = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        self._items[state] = pending
        return state

    def pop(self, state: str) -> PendingSignIn | None:
        self._expire()
        return self._items.pop(state, None)

    def _expire(self) -> None:
        cutoff = time.monotonic() - PENDING_TTL_SECONDS
        for state in [s for s, p in self._items.items() if p.created < cutoff]:
            del self._items[state]

class GitHubClient(ProviderClient):
    @override
    async def authorize_url(self, pending: PendingSignIn, state: str) -> str:
        params = {
            "client_id": self.config.client_id,
            "redirect_uri": pending.redirect_uri,
            "scope": " ".join(self.config.requested_scopes()),
            "state": state,
            "code_challenge": pkce_challenge(pending.verifier),
            "code_challenge_method": "S256",
            "allow_signup": "false",
        }
        return f"{self.config.github_url.rstrip('/')}/login/oauth/authorize?{urlencode(params)}"

    async def _api(self, token: str, path: str) -> Any:
        return await _fetch_json(
            tornado.httpclient.HTTPRequest(
                f"{self.config.github_api_url.rstrip('/')}/{path}",
                headers={
                    "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
                    "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
                    "User-Agent": "woodglue",
                },
            )
        )

    async def _api_all(self, token: str, path: str, max_pages: int = 10) -> list[Any]:
        """All items of a paginated list endpoint, up to `max_pages` of 100."""
        items: list[Any] = []
        for page in range(1, max_pages + 1):
            batch = await self._api(token, f"{path}?per_page=100&page={page}")
            items.extend(batch)
            if len(batch) < 100:
                break
        return items

    @override
    async def complete(self, pending: PendingSignIn, code: str) -> ExternalIdentity:
        tokens = await _fetch_json(
            tornado.httpclient.HTTPRequest(
                f"{self.config.github_url.rstrip('/')}/login/oauth/access_token",
                method="POST",
                headers={"Accept": "application/json"},
                body=urlencode(
                    {
                        "client_id": self.config.client_id,
                        "client_secret": self.config.client_secret,
                        "code": code,
                        "redirect_uri": pending.redirect_uri,
                        "code_verifier": pending.verifier,
                    }
                ),
            )
        )
        token = tokens.get("access_token") if isinstance(tokens, dict) else None
        if not token:
            raise SignInError(f"GitHub did not issue a token: {tokens}")
        user = await self._api(token, "user")
        emails = await self._api(token, "user/emails")
        primary = next((e for e in emails if e.get("primary") and e.get("verified")), None)
        groups: list[str] = []
        if self._needs_groups():
            groups.extend(o["login"] for o in await self._api_all(token, "user/orgs"))
            groups.extend(
                f"{t['organization']['login']}/{t['slug']}"
                for t in await self._api_all(token, "user/teams")
            )
        return ExternalIdentity(
            provider=self.config.id,
            subject=str(user["id"]),
            email=primary["email"] if primary else None,
            email_verified=primary is not None,
            name=str(user.get("name") or user["login"]),
            groups=tuple(groups),
        )

    def _needs_groups(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.config.admit.groups or self.config.group_roles)

docs.text:
Signing keys from a JWKS URL, refreshed hourly and when a token names an unknown key id, but at most once a minute, so forged key ids cannot make woodglue hammer the URL.

https:// keys load in the background (load, which create_app starts), so request handling never waits on the network: a token checked before they arrive, or naming a key not seen yet, is refused while a refresh runs. file:// keys, for providers whose keys are deployed as files, are read in place.

class JwksCache:
    """
    Signing keys from a JWKS URL, refreshed hourly and when a token names an
    unknown key id, but at most once a minute, so forged key ids cannot make
    woodglue hammer the URL.

    `https://` keys load in the background (`load`, which `create_app` starts),
    so request handling never waits on the network: a token checked before
    they arrive, or naming a key not seen yet, is refused while a refresh runs.
    `file://` keys, for providers whose keys are deployed as files, are read
    in place.
    """

    url: str
    _keys: jwt.PyJWKSet | None
    _fetched_at: float
    _loading: asyncio.Task[None] | None

    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        self.url = url
        self._keys = None
        self._fetched_at = -3600.0
        self._loading = None

    @property
    def _is_file(self) -> bool:
        return self.url.startswith("file://")

    def _read_file(self) -> None:
        path = Path(urllib.request.url2pathname(urlsplit(self.url).path))
        try:
            self._keys = jwt.PyJWKSet.from_dict(json.loads(path.read_text()))
        except (OSError, ValueError, jwt.PyJWTError) as exc:
            logger.warning("Could not load signing keys from %s: %s", self.url, exc)

    async def load(self) -> None:
        """Fetch the keys now. Failures are logged; a later check retries."""
        self._fetched_at = time.monotonic()
        if self._is_file:
            self._read_file()
            return
        try:
            raw = await _fetch_json(tornado.httpclient.HTTPRequest(self.url))
            self._keys = jwt.PyJWKSet.from_dict(raw)
        except (ValueError, jwt.PyJWTError, SignInError) as exc:
            logger.warning("Could not load signing keys from %s: %s", self.url, exc)

    def _refresh_soon(self) -> None:
        if time.monotonic() - self._fetched_at < 60:
            return
        if self._loading is not None and not self._loading.done():
            return
        self._fetched_at = time.monotonic()
        if self._is_file:
            self._read_file()
        else:
            self._loading = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self.load())

    def _find(self, kid: str | None) -> jwt.PyJWK | None:
        if self._keys is None:
            return None
        return next((k for k in self._keys.keys if kid is None or k.key_id == kid), None)

    def key(self, kid: str | None) -> jwt.PyJWK:
        found = self._find(kid)
        if found is None or time.monotonic() - self._fetched_at > 3600:
            self._refresh_soon()
            # A file is read in place, so its keys may be here now.
            found = found or self._find(kid)
        if found is None:
            raise SignInError(f"No signing key {kid!r} from {self.url} (yet)")
        return found

class JwtProxy(TrustedProxy):
    """Verifies a JWT the proxy puts in a header, against keys from `jwks_url`."""

    _jwks: JwksCache

    def __init__(self, config: ProviderConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__(config)
        assert config.jwks_url is not None
        self._jwks = JwksCache(config.jwks_url)

    @override
    async def load_keys(self) -> None:
        await self._jwks.load()

    @override
    def identify(self, request: tornado.httputil.HTTPServerRequest) -> ExternalIdentity | None:
        assert self.config.header is not None
        token = request.headers.get(self.config.header)
        if not token:
            return None
        try:
            key = self._jwks.key(jwt.get_unverified_header(token).get("kid"))
            claims: dict[str, Any] = jwt.decode(
                token,
                key,
                algorithms=_ID_TOKEN_ALGORITHMS,
                audience=self.config.audience,
                issuer=self.config.issuer,
                options={"require": ["exp", "sub"]},
            )
        except jwt.PyJWTError as exc:
            raise SignInError(f"Invalid {self.config.header}: {exc}") from exc
        email = claims.get(self.config.email_claim)
        groups = claims.get(self.config.groups_claim) or []
        if isinstance(groups, str):
            groups = [groups]
        return ExternalIdentity(
            provider=self.config.id,
            subject=str(claims["sub"]),
            email=str(email) if email else None,
            # The proxy's own Identity Provider verified the address before signing.
            email_verified=bool(email),
            name=str(claims.get("name") or email or claims["sub"]),
            groups=tuple(str(g) for g in groups),
        )

class HeaderProxy(TrustedProxy):
    """Trusts plain identity headers, but only from `trusted_sources`."""

    _networks: list[ipaddress.IPv4Network | ipaddress.IPv6Network]

    def __init__(self, config: ProviderConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__(config)
        self._networks = [ipaddress.ip_network(s, strict=False) for s in config.trusted_sources]

    def _trusted(self, remote_ip: str | None) -> bool:
        if not remote_ip:
            return False
        try:
            address = ipaddress.ip_address(remote_ip)
        except ValueError:
            return False
        return any(address in network for network in self._networks)

    @override
    def identify(self, request: tornado.httputil.HTTPServerRequest) -> ExternalIdentity | None:
        assert self.config.header is not None
        email = request.headers.get(self.config.header, "").strip()
        if not email:
            return None
        if not self._trusted(request.remote_ip):
            logger.warning(
                "Ignoring %s from untrusted address %s", self.config.header, request.remote_ip
            )
            return None
        name = request.headers.get(self.config.name_header, "") if self.config.name_header else ""
        groups_raw = (
            request.headers.get(self.config.groups_header, "") if self.config.groups_header else ""
        )
        return ExternalIdentity(
            provider=self.config.id,
            subject=email.lower(),
            email=email,
            email_verified=True,
            name=name.strip() or email,
            groups=tuple(g.strip() for g in groups_raw.split(",") if g.strip()),
        )

def admits(rules: AdmitRules, who: ExternalIdentity) -> bool:
    """
    Whether `rules` admit `who`. Email rules only consider a verified email.

    >>> ann = ExternalIdentity("okta", "1", "ann@x.com", True, "Ann", ("ops",))
    >>> admits(AdmitRules(email_domains=["x.com"]), ann), admits(AdmitRules(groups=["ops"]), ann)
    (True, True)
    >>> eve = ExternalIdentity("okta", "2", "eve@x.com", False, "Eve")
    >>> admits(AdmitRules(email_domains=["x.com"]), eve)
    False
    """
    if rules.anyone:
        return True
    email = who.email.lower() if who.email and who.email_verified else None
    if email is not None:
        if email in (e.lower() for e in rules.emails):
            return True
        domain = email.rsplit("@", 1)[-1]
        if domain in (d.lower() for d in rules.email_domains):
            return True
    return any(g in who.groups for g in rules.groups)

def role_sources(
    provider: ProviderConfig, who: ExternalIdentity, admins: list[str]
) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """
    The Role assignments a sign-in sets, keyed by source: the provider's default
    and group-mapped Roles, and `admin` for configured admins.

    >>> p = ProviderConfig(id="okta", kind="oidc", issuer="https://i", client_id="c",
    ...     client_secret="s", admit=AdmitRules(anyone=True), default_roles=["viewer"],
    ...     group_roles={"ops": ["operator"]})
    >>> ann = ExternalIdentity("okta", "1", "ann@x.com", True, "Ann", ("ops",))
    >>> role_sources(p, ann, ["ANN@x.com"])
    {'provider:okta': ['operator', 'viewer'], 'admins': ['admin']}
    """
    roles = set(provider.default_roles)
    for group in who.groups:
        roles.update(provider.group_roles.get(group, []))
    is_admin = bool(who.email and who.email_verified) and (who.email or "").lower() in (
        a.lower() for a in admins
    )
    return {f"provider:{provider.id}": sorted(roles), "admins": [ADMIN_ROLE] if is_admin else []}

class MethodDocHandler(_AuthDocHandler):
    """GET /docs/methods/{prefix}.{module}/{name}.md

    URL uses '/' in place of ':' for cleaner paths. The handler reverses
    this to look up the method by its nsref (which uses ':').
    """

    @override
    def get(self, path: str) -> None:
        method_index = self.visible_index()

        if not path.endswith(".md"):
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(404)
        # Reverse the URL encoding: '/' back to ':'
        name = path[:-3].replace("/", ":")

        dot_pos = name.find(".")
        if dot_pos < 0:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(404)

        prefix = name[:dot_pos]
        method_name = name[dot_pos + 1 :]

        methods = method_index.get(prefix)
        if methods is None:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(404)

        node = methods.get(method_name)
        if node is None:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(404)

        md = generate_method_markdown(prefix, method_name, node)
        self.set_header("Content-Type", "text/markdown; charset=utf-8")
        self.write(md)

def build_method_index(
    namespaces: dict[str, tuple[Namespace, NamespaceEntry]],
) -> dict[str, dict[str, NamespaceNode]]:
    """
    Build a flat lookup: `{prefix: {leaf_name: node}}`.

    Only includes methods tagged with `"api"` from namespaces where
    `expose_api` is True. This resolves the nested namespace structure
    into a simple two-level dict suitable for both RPC dispatch and
    documentation generation.
    """
    index: dict[str, dict[str, NamespaceNode]] = {}
    for prefix, (ns, entry) in namespaces.items():
        if not entry.expose_api:
            continue
        methods: dict[str, NamespaceNode] = {}
        for leaf_name, node in walk_namespace(ns):
            if API_TAG in node.tags:
                methods[leaf_name] = node
        if methods:
            index[prefix] = methods
    return index

def generate_llms_txt(method_index: dict[str, dict[str, NamespaceNode]]) -> str:
    """
    Generate an `llms.txt` index listing all methods in the method index.
    """
    lines = [
        "# Woodglue API",
        "",
        "> JSON-RPC 2.0 server",
        "",
        "## Methods",
        "",
    ]

    for prefix in sorted(method_index):
        for leaf_name, node in sorted(method_index[prefix].items()):
            teaser = _docstring_teaser(node.method.doc)
            qualified = f"{prefix}.{leaf_name}"
            # Replace ':' with '/' in doc URLs for cleaner paths
            doc_path = qualified.replace(":", "/")
            doc_link = f"/docs/methods/{doc_path}.md"
            if teaser:
                lines.append(f"- [{qualified}]({doc_link}): {teaser}")
            else:
                lines.append(f"- [{qualified}]({doc_link})")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def generate_method_markdown(prefix: str, method_name: str, node: NamespaceNode) -> str:
    """
    Generate full markdown documentation for a single method.
    """
    method = node.method
    resolved = _resolve_annotations(method)
    qualified = f"{prefix}.{method_name}"

    doc = method.doc or ""
    full_doc = doc.strip() if doc else ""

    lines = [
        f"# {qualified}",
        "",
        full_doc,
        "",
        "## Parameters",
        "",
        "| Name | Type | Required | Description |",
        "|------|------|----------|-------------|",
    ]

    for arg in method.args:
        ann = resolved.get(arg.name, arg.annotation)
        atype = _type_display(ann)
        required = "no" if arg.is_optional else "yes"
        desc = arg.description or "-"
        lines.append(f"| {arg.name} | {atype} | {required} | {desc} |")

    # Return type
    ret = resolved.get("return", method.return_annotation)
    if ret is not None and ret is not inspect.Parameter.empty:
        lines.extend(["", "## Returns", "", f"`{_type_display(ret)}`"])

    # Referenced models
    models = _collect_referenced_models(method)
    if models:
        lines.extend(["", "## Referenced Models", ""])
        for model in models:
            lines.append(_render_model_table(model))
            lines.append("")

    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def generate_openapi_spec(
    method_index: dict[str, dict[str, NamespaceNode]],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build an OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec dict from the method index."""
    paths: dict[str, Any] = {}

    for prefix in sorted(method_index):
        for leaf_name, node in sorted(method_index[prefix].items()):
            method = node.method
            qualified = f"{prefix}.{leaf_name}"
            path = f"/rpc/{qualified}"

            properties: dict[str, Any] = {}
            required: list[str] = []
            for arg in method.args:
                prop = _python_type_to_schema(arg.annotation)
                if arg.description:
                    prop["description"] = arg.description
                if arg.default is not None and arg.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty:
                    prop["default"] = _json_safe_default(arg.default)
                properties[arg.name] = prop
                if not arg.is_optional:
                    required.append(arg.name)

            request_body_schema: dict[str, Any] = {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": properties,
            }
            if required:
                request_body_schema["required"] = required

            ret = method.return_annotation
            if ret is None or ret is inspect.Parameter.empty:
                response_schema: dict[str, Any] = {"type": "object"}
            else:
                response_schema = _python_type_to_schema(ret)

            summary = _docstring_teaser(method.doc)
            operation: dict[str, Any] = {
                "summary": summary or qualified,
                "operationId": qualified,
                "requestBody": {
                    "required": bool(required),
                    "content": {
                        "application/json": {
                            "schema": request_body_schema,
                        }
                    },
                },
                "responses": {
                    "200": {
                        "description": "Successful response",
                        "content": {
                            "application/json": {
                                "schema": response_schema,
                            }
                        },
                    }
                },
            }
            if method.doc:
                operation["description"] = method.doc.strip()

            paths[path] = {"post": operation}

    return {
        "openapi": "3.0.3",
        "info": {
            "title": "Woodglue JSON-RPC API",
            "version": "1.0.0",
        },
        "paths": paths,
    }

docs.title: woodglue.apps.rpc
docs.text:
JSON-RPC 2.0 handler.

JSON-RPC 2.0 handler backed by a lythonic Namespace.

Dispatches JSON-RPC method calls to NamespaceNode callables, validates parameters against Method.args, and returns standard JSON-RPC 2.0 responses.

Every request runs as a woodglue.access.Caller (see woodglue.apps.authn):

  • No valid credential: -32000 "Unauthorized".
  • A Session-cookie request that is not application/json or comes from another origin: -32003 "Cross-site request rejected".
  • A namespace the Caller cannot see is reported as -32601 "Method not found", so its existence does not leak.
  • A visible namespace without a call Grant: -32003 "Forbidden: ...".
  • DAG runs a call starts, and trigger changes it makes, record the Caller's User id as initiated_by (anonymous when auth is disabled).
  • system.* methods check their own Grants (see woodglue.apps.system_api) and report a missing one as -32003 too.

Errors raised by a node:

  • RpcError (or a subclass) reports an application error to the client: the response error object is {"code": exc.code, "message": exc.message}, plus "data" when exc.data is not None (serialized like results). It is logged at WARNING with the method name, code and message, without a traceback, since it is an expected, client-caused failure.
  • Opt-in is by subclassing only. Any other exception, even one with an integer code attribute (e.g. urllib.error.HTTPError), becomes -32603 "Internal error" with no message leaked to the client, and is logged at ERROR with its traceback.

class RpcError(Exception):
    """
    Application-level JSON-RPC error that a node may raise to report a
    client-visible failure. `str(exc)` is the message.

    Construct as `RpcError(code, message, data=None)`, or set `code` as a
    class attribute on a subclass and construct it from just a message
    (`data` is then keyword-only):

    >>> class NotFound(RpcError):
    ...     code = -32001
    >>> e = NotFound("missing", data={"k": 1})
    >>> (e.code, e.message, e.data, str(e))
    (-32001, 'missing', {'k': 1}, 'missing')
    >>> RpcError(-32010, "x").code
    -32010
    """

    code: int
    message: str
    data: Any

    @overload
    def __init__(self, code: int, message: str, /, data: Any = None) -> None: ...
    @overload
    def __init__(self, message: str, /, *, data: Any = None) -> None: ...
    def __init__(
        self, code_or_message: int | str, message: str | None = None, /, data: Any = None
    ) -> None:
        if isinstance(code_or_message, str):
            if message is not None:
                raise TypeError("RpcError(message, ...) takes `data` only as a keyword")
            class_code = getattr(type(self), "code", None)
            if not isinstance(class_code, int):
                raise TypeError(f"{type(self).__name__} has no class-level `code`; pass one")
            message = code_or_message
        else:
            if message is None:
                raise TypeError("RpcError(code, message) requires a message")
            self.code = code_or_message
        self.message = message
        self.data = data
        super().__init__(message)

class JsonRpcHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """Tornado handler that speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST.

    Expects ``self.application.settings['namespaces']`` to be a dict mapping
    prefix strings to ``lythonic.compose.namespace.Namespace`` instances.
    """

    caller: Caller | None = None

    @override
    def prepare(self) -> None:
        self.set_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        auth = authenticate(self)
        self.caller = auth.caller
        if self.caller is None:
            self._write_unauthorized()
            return
        # A cross-site form or `fetch` cannot send JSON without a CORS preflight,
        # which this server never answers, so the content type blocks most CSRF;
        # the origin check covers the rest.
        if auth.via == AuthVia.cookie and not (
            self.request.headers.get("Content-Type", "").startswith("application/json")
            and is_same_origin(self.request)
        ):
            self.write(_error_response(FORBIDDEN, "Cross-site request rejected"))
            self.finish()

    def _write_unauthorized(self) -> None:
        self.write(
            {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "error": {"code": UNAUTHORIZED, "message": "Unauthorized"},
                "id": None,
            }
        )
        self.finish()

    @override
    async def post(self) -> None:
        request_id: Any = None

        # Parse JSON body
        try:
            body = json.loads(self.request.body)
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
            self.write(_error_response(PARSE_ERROR, "Parse error"))
            return

        # Batch requests are not supported
        if isinstance(body, list):
            self.write(_error_response(INVALID_REQUEST, "Batch requests are not supported"))
            return

        request_id = body.get("id")

        # Validate required fields
        if not isinstance(body, dict) or body.get("jsonrpc") != "2.0" or "method" not in body:
            self.write(
                _error_response(
                    INVALID_REQUEST,
                    "Invalid Request: missing 'jsonrpc' or 'method'",
                    request_id,
                )
            )
            return

        method: str = body["method"]
        params: Any = body.get("params")

        # Resolve namespace and method via dot prefix
        method_index: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = self.application.settings["method_index"]

        dot_pos = method.find(".")
        if dot_pos < 0:
            self.write(_error_response(METHOD_NOT_FOUND, f"Method not found: {method}", request_id))
            return

        prefix = method[:dot_pos]
        method_name = method[dot_pos + 1 :]

        methods = method_index.get(prefix)
        if methods is None:
            self.write(_error_response(METHOD_NOT_FOUND, f"Method not found: {method}", request_id))
            return

        node = methods.get(method_name)
        if node is None or (
            prefix != SYSTEM_PREFIX and self.caller is not None and not self.caller.can_see(prefix)
        ):
            self.write(_error_response(METHOD_NOT_FOUND, f"Method not found: {method}", request_id))
            return
        # System methods check the action they need against the namespace they touch.
        if prefix != SYSTEM_PREFIX and self.caller is not None:
            if not self.caller.can(Action.call, prefix):
                denied = AccessDenied(Action.call, prefix)
                self.write(_error_response(FORBIDDEN, str(denied), request_id))
                return

        # Build kwargs from params
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
        method_args = node.method.args

        if params is not None:
            if isinstance(params, list):
                # Positional params: zip with declared arg names
                for arg_info, value in zip(method_args, params, strict=False):
                    kwargs[arg_info.name] = value
            elif isinstance(params, dict):
                kwargs = dict(params)
            else:
                self.write(
                    _error_response(
                        INVALID_PARAMS,
                        "params must be an array or object",
                        request_id,
                    )
                )
                return

        # Validate required params
        for arg_info in method_args:
            if not arg_info.is_optional and arg_info.name not in kwargs:
                self.write(
                    _error_response(
                        INVALID_PARAMS,
                        f"Missing required parameter: {arg_info.name}",
                        request_id,
                    )
                )
                return

        # Deserialize BaseModel params
        try:
            for arg_info in method_args:
                if (
                    arg_info.name in kwargs
                    and isinstance(arg_info.annotation, type)
                    and issubclass(arg_info.annotation, BaseModel)
                ):
                    kwargs[arg_info.name] = arg_info.annotation.model_validate(
                        kwargs[arg_info.name]
                    )
        except ValidationError as exc:
            self.write(
                _error_response(
                    INVALID_PARAMS,
                    f"Invalid parameters: {exc}",
                    request_id,
                )
            )
            return

        # Set current_mount context var for this namespace
        from woodglue.mount import MountContext, current_mount

        mounts: dict[str, MountContext] = self.application.settings.get("mounts", {})
        mount = mounts.get(prefix)
        token = current_mount.set(mount) if mount else None
        caller_token = current_caller.set(self.caller)

        # Call the method, attributing any runs it starts to the Caller
        try:
            with initiated_by(self.caller.user_id or "anonymous" if self.caller else None):
                result = node(**kwargs)
                if inspect.isawaitable(result):
                    result = await result
        except AccessDenied as exc:
            logger.warning("Access denied calling %s: %s", method, exc)
            self.write(_error_response(FORBIDDEN, str(exc), request_id))
            return
        except RpcError as exc:
            # Expected, client-caused failure: no traceback.
            logger.warning("RPC error calling %s: %d %s", method, exc.code, exc.message)
            self.write(_error_response(exc.code, exc.message, request_id, exc.data))
            return
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Internal error calling %s", method)
            self.write(_error_response(INTERNAL_ERROR, "Internal error", request_id))
            return
        finally:
            current_caller.reset(caller_token)
            if token is not None:
                current_mount.reset(token)

        # Return result
        self.write(
            {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "result": _serialize_result(result),
                "id": request_id,
            }
        )
