def create_app(
    namespaces: dict[str, tuple[Namespace, NamespaceEntry]],
    config: WoodglueConfig | None = None,
    engine_registry: EngineRegistry | None = None,
    mounts: dict[str, MountContext] | None = None,
    auth_store: AuthStore | None = None,
    ui_processes: UiProcesses | None = None,
) -> tornado.web.Application:
    """
    Build a Tornado Application with JSON-RPC and optional docs/UI routes.

    `namespaces` maps prefix strings to `(Namespace, NamespaceEntry)` tuples.
    The plain `Namespace` dict (all namespaces) is stored in app settings for
    internal use. The `method_index` is filtered by `expose_api`.

    With auth enabled, `auth_store` defaults to one opened on
    `config.storage.auth_db`, which must then be set; pass it to share the
    instance the system namespace uses. Without `config`, auth is disabled. `ui_processes` supervises Process-backed UIs; the caller
    starts and stops it (see `wgl start`).
    """
    if config is None:
        config = WoodglueConfig(namespaces={}, auth=AuthConfig(enabled=False))
    if auth_store is None and config.auth.enabled:
        if config.storage.auth_db is None:
            raise ValueError("Auth is enabled but storage.auth_db is not set")
        auth_store = AuthStore(config.storage.auth_db, config.auth.resolved_roles())

    # Plain namespace dict for internal use (e.g. `wgl run`)
    plain_namespaces = {prefix: ns for prefix, (ns, _) in namespaces.items()}

    method_index = build_method_index(namespaces)

    handlers: list[Any] = [
        (r"/rpc", JsonRpcHandler),
    ]

    if config.docs.enabled:
        from woodglue.apps.llm_docs import LlmsTxtHandler, MethodDocHandler, OpenApiHandler

        handlers.append((r"/docs/llms\.txt", LlmsTxtHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/docs/methods/(.+)", MethodDocHandler))
        if config.docs.openapi:
            handlers.append((r"/docs/openapi\.json", OpenApiHandler))

    login_providers: Mapping[str, ProviderClient] = {}
    if auth_store is not None:
        from woodglue.apps.auth_pages import (
            CliAuthorizeHandler,
            CliTokenHandler,
            LoginHandler,
            LogoutHandler,
            SignInCallbackHandler,
            StartSignInHandler,
        )

        login_providers = make_clients(config.auth.providers)
        handlers.append((r"/auth/login", LoginHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/auth/logout", LogoutHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/auth/start/([^/]+)", StartSignInHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/auth/callback/([^/]+)", SignInCallbackHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/auth/verify", VerifyHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/auth/cli", CliAuthorizeHandler))
        handlers.append((r"/auth/cli/token", CliTokenHandler))

    if config.ui.enabled:
        console_dist = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "ui" / "dist"
        if console_dist.is_dir():
            handlers.append((r"/console", tornado.web.RedirectHandler, {"url": "/console/"}))
            handlers.append(
                (
                    r"/console/(.*)",
                    UiStaticHandler,
                    {"path": str(console_dist), "default_filename": "index.html"},
                )
            )

    if ui_processes is None:
        ui_processes = UiProcesses(config.uis, "")
    for name, entry in config.uis.items():
        handlers.append((rf"/ui/{name}", tornado.web.RedirectHandler, {"url": f"/ui/{name}/"}))
        if not entry.is_static:
            handlers.append(
                (rf"/ui/{name}/.*", UiProxyHandler, {"ui_name": name, "public": entry.public})
            )
            continue
        assert entry.path is not None
        if not Path(entry.path).is_dir():
            logger.warning("UI '%s': directory %s does not exist", name, entry.path)
        handlers.append(
            (
                rf"/ui/{name}/(.*)",
                UiStaticHandler,
                {
                    "path": entry.path,
                    "default_filename": "index.html",
                    "ui_name": name,
                    "spa_fallback": entry.spa_fallback,
                    "public": entry.public,
                },
            )
        )

    if config.ui.enabled or config.uis:
        handlers.append((r"/", tornado.web.RedirectHandler, {"url": ui_path(config.ui.default)}))

    trusted_proxies = make_trusted_proxies(config.auth.providers) if auth_store else []
    for proxy in trusted_proxies:
        tornado.ioloop.IOLoop.current().add_callback(proxy.load_keys)

    return tornado.web.Application(
        handlers,
        namespaces=plain_namespaces,
        method_index=method_index,
        config=config,
        auth_enabled=config.auth.enabled,
        auth_store=auth_store,
        login_providers=login_providers,
        trusted_proxies=trusted_proxies,
        pending_sign_ins=PendingSignIns(),
        cli_codes=CliCodes(),
        ui_processes=ui_processes,
        ui_sockets=UiSockets(),
        engine_registry=engine_registry,
        mounts=mounts or {},
    )

docs.title: woodglue.apps.ui_process
docs.text:
Supervising the processes behind Process-backed UIs.

Supervising the processes behind Process-backed UIs.

For each UI with kind or command (see woodglue.config.UiEntry), UiProcesses runs the process on a free loopback port and keeps it running:

  • Started by wgl start after the engines, and stopped (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period) with them.
  • Ready once an HTTP request to ready_path gets any non-5xx answer; until then the proxy answers 503.
  • Restarted after it exits, waiting 1s, 2s, 4s, ... up to a minute between attempts; the wait resets once a run has stayed up for a minute. While it is down its state is failed, which system.list_uis reports.
  • Its stdout and stderr go to the log as woodglue.ui.<name>.

The process environment adds the UI's env and WOODGLUE_URL, the loopback address of the woodglue API.

An upstream UI has no process; UiProcesses.upstream returns its URL as is.

    _changed: asyncio.Condition

    def __init__(self, name: str, entry: UiEntry, woodglue_url: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.entry = entry
        self.woodglue_url = woodglue_url
        self.state = UiState.stopped
        self.port = None
        self.pid = None
        self.generation = 0
        self._log = logging.getLogger(f"woodglue.ui.{name}")
        self._proc = None
        self._task = None
        self._stopping = False
        self._changed = asyncio.Condition()

    @property
    def upstream(self) -> str | None:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}" if self.state == UiState.ready else None

    async def _set_state(self, state: UiState) -> None:
        async with self._changed:
            self.state = state
            if state == UiState.ready:
                self.generation += 1
            self._changed.notify_all()

    async def wait_ready(self) -> None:
        async with self._changed:
            await self._changed.wait_for(lambda: self.state == UiState.ready)

    async def wait_restarted(self) -> None:
        """Wait until a run after the current one is ready."""
        async with self._changed:
            current = self.generation
            await self._changed.wait_for(
                lambda: self.generation > current and self.state == UiState.ready
            )

    def start(self) -> None:
        self._stopping = False
        self._task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._supervise())

    async def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stopping = True
        proc = self._proc
        if proc is not None and proc.returncode is None:
            proc.terminate()
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), _STOP_GRACE_SECONDS)
            except TimeoutError:
                self._log.warning("Did not exit after SIGTERM; killing it")
                proc.kill()
                await proc.wait()
        if self._task is not None:
            self._task.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await self._task
        await self._set_state(UiState.stopped)

    async def _supervise(self) -> None:
        backoff = 1.0
        while not self._stopping:
            started = time.monotonic()
            await self._run_once()
            if self._stopping:
                return
            if time.monotonic() - started >= _STABLE_SECONDS:
                backoff = 1.0
            await self._set_state(UiState.failed)
            self._log.warning("Exited; restarting in %.0fs", backoff)
            await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
            backoff = min(backoff * 2, _MAX_BACKOFF_SECONDS)

    async def _run_once(self) -> None:
        await self._set_state(UiState.starting)
        self.port = _free_port()
        command = ui_command(self.name, self.entry, self.port)
        env = {**os.environ, **self.entry.env, "WOODGLUE_URL": self.woodglue_url}
        try:
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                *command,
                cwd=self.entry.cwd,
                env=env,
                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
            )
        except OSError as exc:
            self._log.error("Could not start %s: %s", command[0], exc)
            return
        self._proc = proc
        self.pid = proc.pid
        self._log.info("Started pid %d on port %d", proc.pid, self.port)
        pump = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._pump_output(proc))
        probe = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._probe(proc))
        returncode = await proc.wait()
        probe.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(pump, probe, return_exceptions=True)
        if not self._stopping:
            self._log.warning("pid %d exited with status %s", proc.pid, returncode)

    async def _pump_output(self, proc: asyncio.subprocess.Process) -> None:
        assert proc.stdout is not None
        async for line in proc.stdout:
            self._log.info("%s", line.decode(errors="replace").rstrip())

    async def _probe(self, proc: asyncio.subprocess.Process) -> None:
        url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}{ready_path(self.name, self.entry)}"
        client = tornado.httpclient.AsyncHTTPClient()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + _STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
        while proc.returncode is None:
            try:
                resp = await client.fetch(
                    url, raise_error=False, follow_redirects=False, request_timeout=2
                )
                if resp.code < 500:
                    await self._set_state(UiState.ready)
                    return
            except OSError:
                pass
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                self._log.error("Not ready after %.0fs; stopping it", _STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
                proc.terminate()
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)

        """Where to proxy a UI's requests now, or `None` while its process is not ready."""
        if name in self._upstreams:

        process = self._processes.get(name)

def ui_command(name: str, entry: UiEntry, port: int) -> list[str]:
    """
    The command line for a supervised UI.

    >>> e = UiEntry(command=["srv", "--port={port}", "--root={base_path}"])
    >>> ui_command("dash", e, 8601)
    ['srv', '--port=8601', '--root=/ui/dash']
    >>> cmd = ui_command("dash", UiEntry(kind="streamlit", app="app.py"), 8601)
    >>> cmd[1:5], cmd[5:8]
    (['-m', 'streamlit', 'run', 'app.py'], ['--server.port=8601', '--server.address=127.0.0.1', '--server.baseUrlPath=ui/dash'])
    """
    base_path = f"/ui/{name}"
    if entry.kind == UiKind.streamlit:
        assert entry.app is not None
        dev = "true" if entry.dev else "false"
        return [
            sys.executable,
            "-m",
            "streamlit",
            "run",
            entry.app,
            f"--server.port={port}",
            "--server.address=127.0.0.1",
            f"--server.baseUrlPath={base_path.lstrip('/')}",
            "--server.headless=true",
            "--browser.gatherUsageStats=false",
            f"--server.runOnSave={dev}",
            f"--server.fileWatcherType={'auto' if entry.dev else 'none'}",
        ]
    assert entry.command is not None
    return [arg.format(port=port, base_path=base_path) for arg in entry.command]

docs.text:
Reverse proxy for Process-backed UIs.

Reverse proxy for Process-backed UIs at /ui/<name>/, for HTTP and websockets.

Requests keep their full path (/ui/<name>/...) and Host header, so the UI process must serve under its base path, as woodglue.apps.ui_process sets up for Streamlit. Before forwarding, the proxy:

  • checks view on ui:<name> like any UI (see woodglue.apps.uis);
  • removes the woodglue Session cookie, keeping the app's own cookies such as Streamlit's _streamlit_xsrf, so the process never holds a credential that outlives the Session (see docs/adr/0003);
  • removes Authorization and any client-sent X-Woodglue-* header;
  • adds X-Woodglue-User (JSON with id, name, email, roles) and, for a browser Session, X-Woodglue-Token, a Delegated Token the process uses to call the API as that User, limited to the UI's grants (see woodglue.ui_support).

Response bodies pass through as they arrive, so event streams and long polls work; request bodies are read in full first.

Websockets opened under a Session are closed when it ends: at once on logout, and within SWEEP_SECONDS when it expires or its User is disabled.

class UiSockets:
    """Open proxied websockets by Session, so they can be closed when it ends."""

    _by_session: dict[str, set[UiProxyHandler]]
    _sweeper: tornado.ioloop.PeriodicCallback | None

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._by_session = {}
        self._sweeper = None

    def add(self, session_secret: str, handler: UiProxyHandler) -> None:
        self._by_session.setdefault(session_secret, set()).add(handler)
        if self._sweeper is None:
            self._sweeper = tornado.ioloop.PeriodicCallback(self._sweep, SWEEP_SECONDS * 1000)
            self._sweeper.start()

    def remove(self, session_secret: str, handler: UiProxyHandler) -> None:
        handlers = self._by_session.get(session_secret)
        if handlers is not None:
            handlers.discard(handler)
            if not handlers:
                del self._by_session[session_secret]

    def close_session(self, session_secret: str) -> None:
        for handler in list(self._by_session.pop(session_secret, ())):
            handler.close(1008, "Session ended")

    def _sweep(self) -> None:
        for secret, handlers in list(self._by_session.items()):
            store: AuthStore | None = next(iter(handlers)).application.settings.get("auth_store")
            if store is not None and not store.session_is_live(secret):
                self.close_session(secret)

class UiProxyHandler(tornado.websocket.WebSocketHandler):
    """Proxies one Process-backed UI; a websocket upgrade switches to frame relaying."""

    SUPPORTED_METHODS: tuple[str, ...] = (
        "GET",
        "HEAD",
        "POST",
        "PUT",
        "PATCH",
        "DELETE",
        "OPTIONS",
    )  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleVariableOverride]

    ui_name: str = ""
    public: bool = False
    auth: Authentication | None = None
    _upstream_ws: tornado.websocket.WebSocketClientConnection | None = None
    _client_subprotocols: list[str] | None = None
    _relay: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None

    @override
    def initialize(self, ui_name: str, public: bool = False) -> None:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        self.ui_name = ui_name
        self.public = public

    @override
    def prepare(self) -> None:
        self.auth = authenticate(self) if self.public else require_view(self, self.ui_name)

    def _upstream_base(self) -> str | None:
        processes: UiProcesses = self.application.settings["ui_processes"]
        return processes.upstream(self.ui_name)

    def _upstream_headers(self) -> tornado.httputil.HTTPHeaders:
        headers = tornado.httputil.HTTPHeaders()
        for name, value in self.request.headers.get_all():
            lower = name.lower()
            if lower in _NOT_FORWARDED or lower.startswith(("x-woodglue-", "sec-websocket-")):
                continue
            headers.add(name, value)
        cookie = strip_cookie(self.request.headers.get("Cookie", ""), SESSION_COOKIE)
        if cookie:
            headers["Cookie"] = cookie
        headers["X-Forwarded-Proto"] = public_scheme(self)
        headers["X-Forwarded-Host"] = self.request.host
        if self.request.remote_ip:
            headers["X-Forwarded-For"] = self.request.remote_ip
        if self.auth is not None:
            store: AuthStore | None = self.application.settings.get("auth_store")
            entry = self.application.settings["config"].uis.get(self.ui_name)
            grants = entry.grants if entry is not None else None
            for name, value in identity_headers(self.auth, store, self.ui_name, grants).items():
                headers[name] = value
        return headers

    # HTTP

    @override
    async def get(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        if self.request.headers.get("Upgrade", "").lower() == "websocket":
            await super().get(*args, **kwargs)
        else:
            await self._proxy_http()

    @override
    def head(self, *args: Any) -> Awaitable[None]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        return self._proxy_http()

    @override
    def post(self, *args: Any) -> Awaitable[None]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        return self._proxy_http()

    @override
    def put(self, *args: Any) -> Awaitable[None]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        return self._proxy_http()

    @override
    def patch(self, *args: Any) -> Awaitable[None]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        return self._proxy_http()

    @override
    def delete(self, *args: Any) -> Awaitable[None]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        return self._proxy_http()

    @override
    def options(self, *args: Any) -> Awaitable[None]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
        return self._proxy_http()

    async def _proxy_http(self) -> None:
        base = self._upstream_base()
        if base is None:
            self.set_status(503)
            self.finish(f"UI '{self.ui_name}' is starting or unavailable; try again shortly")
            return
        method = self.request.method or "GET"
        relay = _ResponseRelay(self, method)
        request = tornado.httpclient.HTTPRequest(
            f"{base}{self.request.uri}",
            method=method,
            headers=self._upstream_headers(),
            body=self.request.body if method not in ("GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS") else None,
            follow_redirects=False,
            decompress_response=False,
            allow_nonstandard_methods=True,
            connect_timeout=10,
            # No overall limit: event streams and long polls stay open as long as the UI wants.
            request_timeout=0,
            header_callback=relay.on_header_line,
            streaming_callback=relay.on_chunk,
        )
        try:
            resp = await tornado.httpclient.AsyncHTTPClient().fetch(request, raise_error=False)
            failed = resp.code == 599
        except OSError as exc:
            logger.warning("UI '%s' upstream failed: %s", self.ui_name, exc)
            failed = True
        if failed and not relay.started:
            self.set_status(502)
            self.finish(f"UI '{self.ui_name}' did not answer")
            return
        self.finish()

    # Websockets

    @override
    def select_subprotocol(self, subprotocols: list[str]) -> str | None:
        self._client_subprotocols = subprotocols
        return subprotocols[0] if subprotocols else None

    @override
    async def open(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        base = self._upstream_base()
        if base is None:
            self.close(1013, "UI is starting or unavailable")
            return
        ws_base = "ws" + base[len("http") :]
        request = tornado.httpclient.HTTPRequest(
            f"{ws_base}{self.request.uri}", headers=self._upstream_headers()
        )
        try:
            self._upstream_ws = await tornado.websocket.websocket_connect(
                request, subprotocols=self._client_subprotocols
            )
        except (OSError, tornado.httpclient.HTTPClientError) as exc:
            logger.warning("UI '%s' websocket upstream failed: %s", self.ui_name, exc)
            self.close(1011, "UI did not accept the connection")
            return
        if self.auth is not None and self.auth.session_secret:
            sockets: UiSockets = self.application.settings["ui_sockets"]
            sockets.add(self.auth.session_secret, self)
        self._relay = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._relay_upstream())

    async def _relay_upstream(self) -> None:
        upstream = self._upstream_ws
        assert upstream is not None
        while True:
            message = await upstream.read_message()
            if message is None:
                self.close()
                return
            try:
                await self.write_message(message, binary=isinstance(message, bytes))
            except tornado.websocket.WebSocketClosedError:
                return

    @override
    async def on_message(self, message: str | bytes) -> None:
        if self._upstream_ws is not None:
            await self._upstream_ws.write_message(message, binary=isinstance(message, bytes))

    @override
    def on_close(self) -> None:
        if self._upstream_ws is not None:
            self._upstream_ws.close()
        if self.auth is not None and self.auth.session_secret:
            sockets: UiSockets = self.application.settings["ui_sockets"]
            sockets.remove(self.auth.session_secret, self)

def strip_cookie(header: str, name: str) -> str:
    """
    Remove one cookie from a `Cookie` header, keeping the rest as sent.

    >>> strip_cookie("a=1; wgl_session=s; b=2", "wgl_session")
    'a=1; b=2'

    ''

    return "; ".join(p for p in kept if p)

class VerifyHandler(tornado.web.RequestHandler):
    """
    GET `/auth/verify`: access check for a reverse proxy's `forward_auth`
    (see `docs/adr/0004`). The UI is `?ui=<name>`, or taken from the
    `X-Forwarded-Uri` the proxy sends (`/ui/<name>/...` or `/console/...`).

    Answers 200 with the identity headers for an allowed request, a redirect to
    the login page (returning to the original URI) without a Session, 403
    without the `view` Grant, and 400 if no UI can be named.
    """

    @override
    def get(self) -> None:
        uri = self.request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-Uri", "/")
        name = self.get_argument("ui", None) or _ui_name_from_path(uri)
        if name is None:
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(400, "No UI named by ?ui= or X-Forwarded-Uri")
        settings = self.application.settings
        entry = settings["config"].uis.get(name)
        auth = authenticate(self)
        if auth.caller is None and not (entry is not None and entry.public):
            self.redirect(f"/auth/login?next={quote(uri, safe='')}")
            return
        public = entry is not None and entry.public
        if (
            not public
            and auth.caller is not None
            and not auth.caller.can(Action.view, f"ui:{name}")
        ):
            raise tornado.web.HTTPError(403)
        grants = entry.grants if entry is not None else None
        for header, value in identity_headers(
            auth, settings.get("auth_store"), name, grants
        ).items():
            self.set_header(header, value)
        self.set_status(200)

    grants: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    The headers that tell a UI's server who is viewing (see
    `woodglue.ui_support`): the User as JSON, and for a browser Session a
    Delegated Token for this UI, narrowed to the UI's `grants`.
    """
    headers: dict[str, str] = {}
    caller = auth.caller
    if caller is not None:
        headers[USER_HEADER] = json.dumps(
            {
                "id": caller.user_id,
                "name": caller.name,
                "email": caller.email,
                "roles": list(caller.roles),
            }
        )
    if store is not None and auth.via == AuthVia.cookie and auth.session_secret:
        try:
            headers[TOKEN_HEADER] = store.delegate(auth.session_secret, ui_name, grants)
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return headers

def require_view(handler: tornado.web.RequestHandler, ui_name: str) -> Authentication | None:
    """
    Check that the request may open `ui_name`, finishing it with a login
    redirect or 403 if not. Returns the request's `Authentication`, or `None`
    once the request is finished.
    """
    auth = authenticate(handler)
    if auth.caller is None:
        handler.redirect(f"/auth/login?next={quote(handler.request.uri or '/', safe='')}")
        return None
    if not auth.caller.can(Action.view, f"ui:{ui_name}"):
        handler.set_status(403)
        handler.finish(f"Forbidden: requires 'view' on 'ui:{ui_name}'")
        return None
    return auth

Users, Role assignments, and credentials in auth.db.

AuthStore is the only reader and writer of auth.db. Credentials are opaque random secrets looked up on every request (see docs/adr/0002), so revoking a token, disabling a User, or changing a Role assignment takes effect immediately, including on a running server.

Role definitions are not stored here: they come from woodglue.yaml (see woodglue.access). A Role assignment naming a Role that is no longer defined grants nothing.

A Session is the credential behind a browser's cookie. It ends after session_idle without use or session_max after creation, whichever is first; woodglue does not re-check with the Identity Provider in between.

A Delegated Token lets a Process-backed UI call the API as the User viewing it. It belongs to one Session and one UI, carries the Session's Grants narrowed to the UI's own grants, and ends with the Session. Its use does not keep the Session alive: only the person's own requests, including those through the UI, do.

The built-in admin Service User owns the tokens that wgl token prints. Tokens from the pre-Users tokens table are migrated to it on first open, so existing scripts keep working.

class AuthStore:
    """
    Access to `auth.db`. `roles` maps Role names to their Grants, as returned
    by `woodglue.access.resolve_roles`.
    """

    db_path: Path
    roles: dict[str, tuple[Grant, ...]]
    session_idle: timedelta
    session_max: timedelta
    clock: Callable[[], datetime]

    def __init__(
        self,
        db_path: Path,
        roles: dict[str, tuple[Grant, ...]],
        *,
        session_idle: timedelta = DEFAULT_SESSION_IDLE,
        session_max: timedelta = DEFAULT_SESSION_MAX,
        clock: Callable[[], datetime] = _now,
    ) -> None:
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.roles = roles
        self.session_idle = session_idle
        self.session_max = session_max
        self.clock = clock
        with self._connect() as conn:
            self._migrate(conn)

    @contextmanager
    def _connect(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)) as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
            yield conn
            conn.commit()

    def _migrate(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        if conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0] >= _SCHEMA_VERSION:
            return
        conn.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE users (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                email TEXT UNIQUE,
                kind TEXT NOT NULL,
                disabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE role_assignments (
                user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
                role TEXT NOT NULL,
                source TEXT NOT NULL,
                PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role, source)
            );
            CREATE TABLE linked_identities (
                provider TEXT NOT NULL,
                subject TEXT NOT NULL,
                user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                PRIMARY KEY (provider, subject)
            );
            CREATE TABLE credentials (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                secret TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                kind TEXT NOT NULL,
                user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                grants TEXT,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                expires_at TEXT,
                last_used_at TEXT,
                parent_id TEXT REFERENCES credentials(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
            );
            """
        )
        self._ensure_admin_user(conn)
        # Before 0.0.9, auth.db held only a list of tokens, all with full access.
        has_legacy = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'tokens'"
        ).fetchone()
        if has_legacy:
            for row in conn.execute("SELECT token, created_at FROM tokens ORDER BY created_at"):
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO credentials (id, secret, kind, user_id, name, created_at) "
                    + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (
                        _new_id("tok"),
                        row["token"],
                        CredentialKind.token,
                        ADMIN_USER_ID,
                        "wgl token",
                        row["created_at"],
                    ),
                )
            conn.execute("DROP TABLE tokens")
        conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {_SCHEMA_VERSION}")

    def _ensure_admin_user(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (id, name, kind, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (ADMIN_USER_ID, ADMIN_USER_ID, UserKind.service, self.clock().isoformat()),
        )
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO role_assignments (user_id, role, source) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (ADMIN_USER_ID, ADMIN_ROLE, MANUAL),
        )

    # Users

    def _user_from_row(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, row: sqlite3.Row) -> User:
        roles = [
            r["role"]
            for r in conn.execute(
                "SELECT DISTINCT role FROM role_assignments WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY role",
                (row["id"],),
            )
        ]
        return User(
            id=row["id"],
            name=row["name"],
            email=row["email"],
            kind=UserKind(row["kind"]),
            disabled=bool(row["disabled"]),
            roles=roles,
            created_at=datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]),
        )

    def list_users(self) -> list[User]:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY created_at, id").fetchall()
            return [self._user_from_row(conn, r) for r in rows]

    def find_user(self, ref: str) -> User:
        """
        Look up a User by id, email, or name. A name matching several Users is
        ambiguous and raises `UnknownUser`.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? OR email = ?", (ref, ref)
            ).fetchall()
            if not rows:
                rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", (ref,)).fetchall()
            if len(rows) != 1:
                raise UnknownUser(f"No unique User matches {ref!r}")
            return self._user_from_row(conn, rows[0])

    def create_service_user(self, name: str) -> User:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            taken = conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE name = ? OR id = ?", (name, name)
            ).fetchone()
            if taken:
                raise ValueError(f"A User named {name!r} already exists")
            user_id = _new_id("svc")
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO users (id, name, kind, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (user_id, name, UserKind.service, self.clock().isoformat()),
            )
            row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone()
            return self._user_from_row(conn, row)

    def assign_role(self, user_id: str, role: str) -> None:
        if role not in self.roles:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown Role {role!r}; defined: {', '.join(sorted(self.roles))}")
        with self._connect() as conn:
            self._require_user(conn, user_id)
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO role_assignments (user_id, role, source) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                (user_id, role, MANUAL),
            )

    def unassign_role(self, user_id: str, role: str) -> None:
        """Remove a Role from every source; a provider re-adds its own at the next sign-in."""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            self._require_user(conn, user_id)
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM role_assignments WHERE user_id = ? AND role = ?", (user_id, role)
            )

    def set_disabled(self, user_id: str, disabled: bool) -> None:
        """Disable or re-enable a User. Disabling deletes all of its credentials."""
        if disabled and user_id == ADMIN_USER_ID:
            raise ValueError("The built-in admin User cannot be disabled")
        with self._connect() as conn:
            self._require_user(conn, user_id)
            conn.execute("UPDATE users SET disabled = ? WHERE id = ?", (int(disabled), user_id))
            if disabled:
                conn.execute("DELETE FROM credentials WHERE user_id = ?", (user_id,))

    def linked_user(self, provider: str, subject: str) -> str | None:
        """The id of the User linked to an Identity Provider's subject, if any."""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT user_id FROM linked_identities WHERE provider = ? AND subject = ?",
                (provider, subject),
            ).fetchone()
        return row["user_id"] if row else None

    def sign_in_person(
        self,
        provider: str,
        subject: str,
        *,
        email: str | None,
        email_verified: bool,
        name: str,
        role_sources: dict[str, list[str]],
    ) -> User:
        """
        Find or create the User for an Identity Provider's assertion, after the
        caller has decided the person is admitted.

        The User is found by its Linked Identity, else by a verified email
        matching an existing User (linking the identity to it), else created.
        An unverified email is not stored, so it can never take over an account.
        Each entry of `role_sources` replaces that source's Role assignments,
        leaving assignments from other sources (and manual ones) alone.

        Raises `UserDisabled` if the User is disabled.
        """
        verified_email = email.lower() if email and email_verified else None
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT u.* FROM linked_identities l JOIN users u ON u.id = l.user_id "
                + "WHERE l.provider = ? AND l.subject = ?",
                (provider, subject),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None and verified_email is not None:
                row = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ? AND kind = ?",
                    (verified_email, UserKind.person),
                ).fetchone()
            now = self.clock().isoformat()
            if row is None:
                user_id = _new_id("usr")
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO users (id, name, email, kind, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (user_id, name, verified_email, UserKind.person, now),
                )
            else:
                user_id = row["id"]
                if row["disabled"]:
                    raise UserDisabled(f"User {user_id} is disabled")
                conn.execute("UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?", (name, user_id))
                if verified_email and row["email"] != verified_email:
                    taken = conn.execute(
                        "SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE email = ?", (verified_email,)
                    ).fetchone()
                    if not taken:
                        conn.execute(
                            "UPDATE users SET email = ? WHERE id = ?", (verified_email, user_id)
                        )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO linked_identities (provider, subject, user_id, created_at) "
                + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (provider, subject, user_id, now),
            )
            for source, roles in role_sources.items():
                conn.execute(
                    "DELETE FROM role_assignments WHERE user_id = ? AND source = ?",
                    (user_id, source),
                )
                for role in roles:
                    if role not in self.roles:
                        logger.warning("Sign-in source %s names undefined Role %r", source, role)
                        continue
                    conn.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO role_assignments (user_id, role, source) "
                        + "VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                        (user_id, role, source),
                    )
            user_row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone()
            return self._user_from_row(conn, user_row)

    def _require_user(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, user_id: str) -> None:
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone():
            raise UnknownUser(f"No User with id {user_id!r}")

    # Personal Access Tokens

    def create_token(
        self,
        user_id: str,
        name: str,
        *,
        expires_at: datetime | None = None,
        grants: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> IssuedToken:
        """
        Issue a Personal Access Token. `grants`, if given, narrows the token to
        a subset of its User's Grants; they are validated but not checked
        against the User, since the effective set is computed per request.
        """
        if grants is not None:
            grants = [str(Grant.parse(g)) for g in grants]
        with self._connect() as conn:
            self._require_user(conn, user_id)
            return self._insert_token(conn, user_id, name, expires_at, grants)

    def _insert_token(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        user_id: str,
        name: str,
        expires_at: datetime | None = None,
        grants: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> IssuedToken:
        issued = IssuedToken(id=_new_id("tok"), secret=secrets.token_urlsafe(32))
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO credentials "
            + "(id, secret, kind, user_id, name, grants, created_at, expires_at) "
            + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (
                issued.id,
                issued.secret,
                CredentialKind.token,
                user_id,
                name,
                json.dumps(grants) if grants is not None else None,
                self.clock().isoformat(),
                expires_at.isoformat() if expires_at else None,
            ),
        )
        return issued

    def list_tokens(self, user_id: str | None = None) -> list[TokenInfo]:
        query = "SELECT * FROM credentials WHERE kind = ?"
        params: list[str] = [CredentialKind.token]
        if user_id is not None:
            query += " AND user_id = ?"
            params.append(user_id)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(query + " ORDER BY created_at, id", params).fetchall()
        return [
            TokenInfo(
                id=r["id"],
                user_id=r["user_id"],
                name=r["name"],
                grants=json.loads(r["grants"]) if r["grants"] else None,
                created_at=datetime.fromisoformat(r["created_at"]),
                expires_at=_parse_time(r["expires_at"]),
            )
            for r in rows
        ]

    def token_owner(self, token_id: str) -> str | None:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT user_id FROM credentials WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?",
                (token_id, CredentialKind.token),
            ).fetchone()
        return row["user_id"] if row else None

    def revoke_token(self, token_id: str) -> bool:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cur = conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM credentials WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?",
                (token_id, CredentialKind.token),
            )
            return cur.rowcount > 0

    def ensure_admin_token(self) -> None:
        """Create a token for the built-in admin User if it has none."""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            if not self._admin_secrets(conn):
                self._insert_token(conn, ADMIN_USER_ID, "wgl token")

    def admin_tokens(self) -> list[str]:
        """Secrets of the admin User's tokens, oldest first."""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            return self._admin_secrets(conn)

    def _admin_secrets(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> list[str]:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT secret FROM credentials WHERE user_id = ? AND kind = ? "
            + "ORDER BY created_at, id",
            (ADMIN_USER_ID, CredentialKind.token),
        ).fetchall()
        return [r["secret"] for r in rows]

    def rotate_admin_token(self) -> str:
        """
        Replace all admin tokens with one new one, in one transaction, so a
        concurrent `resolve` never sees the admin without a token.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM credentials WHERE user_id = ? AND kind = ?",
                (ADMIN_USER_ID, CredentialKind.token),
            )
            return self._insert_token(conn, ADMIN_USER_ID, "wgl token").secret

    # Sessions

    def live_session(self, user_id: str, name: str) -> str | None:
        """The secret of a live Session of `user_id` started under `name`, if any."""
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT secret FROM credentials WHERE user_id = ? AND kind = ? AND name = ? "
                + "ORDER BY created_at DESC",
                (user_id, CredentialKind.session, name),
            ).fetchall()
        return next((r["secret"] for r in rows if self.session_is_live(r["secret"])), None)

    def create_session(self, user_id: str, name: str = "browser") -> str:
        """
        Start a Session for a User and return its secret, for the browser
        cookie. `name` records how it was started.
        """
        now = self.clock()
        secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        with self._connect() as conn:
            self._require_user(conn, user_id)
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO credentials "
                + "(id, secret, kind, user_id, name, created_at, expires_at, last_used_at) "
                + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    _new_id("ses"),
                    secret,
                    CredentialKind.session,
                    user_id,
                    name,
                    now.isoformat(),
                    (now + self.session_max).isoformat(),
                    now.isoformat(),
                ),
            )
        return secret

    def delegate(self, session_secret: str, ui_name: str, grants: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
        """
        The Delegated Token for a UI acting on behalf of a Session, created on
        first use. `grants`, the UI's configured Grants, narrows it like a
        narrowed Personal Access Token, and is updated on each call so a config
        change applies at once. Raises `ValueError` unless `session_secret` is
        a live Session.
        """
        grants_json = (
            json.dumps([str(Grant.parse(g)) for g in grants]) if grants is not None else None
        )
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM credentials WHERE secret = ? AND kind = ?",
                (session_secret, CredentialKind.session),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None or not self._session_alive(conn, row, self.clock()):
                raise ValueError("Only a live Session can be delegated")
            existing = conn.execute(
                "SELECT secret FROM credentials WHERE parent_id = ? AND kind = ? AND name = ?",
                (row["id"], CredentialKind.delegated, ui_name),
            ).fetchone()
            if existing is not None:
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE credentials SET grants = ? WHERE secret = ?",
                    (grants_json, existing["secret"]),
                )
                return existing["secret"]
            secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO credentials "
                + "(id, secret, kind, user_id, name, grants, created_at, parent_id) "
                + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    _new_id("dlg"),
                    secret,
                    CredentialKind.delegated,
                    row["user_id"],
                    ui_name,
                    grants_json,
                    self.clock().isoformat(),
                    row["id"],
                ),
            )
            return secret

    def _session_alive(
        self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, row: sqlite3.Row, now: datetime, *, use: bool = True
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Apply a Session's limits, deleting it (and its Delegated Tokens) once it
        has expired, and with `use`, record that it was used.
        """
        expires_at = _parse_time(row["expires_at"])
        last_used = _parse_time(row["last_used_at"]) or now
        if (expires_at is not None and expires_at <= now) or last_used + self.session_idle <= now:
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM credentials WHERE id = ?", (row["id"],))
            return False
        if use and now - last_used >= _TOUCH_INTERVAL:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE credentials SET last_used_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
                (now.isoformat(), row["id"]),
            )
        return True

    def session_is_live(self, secret: str) -> bool:
        """Whether a Session is still valid, without counting this check as use."""
        now = self.clock()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT c.expires_at, c.last_used_at, u.disabled FROM credentials c "
                + "JOIN users u ON u.id = c.user_id WHERE c.secret = ? AND c.kind = ?",
                (secret, CredentialKind.session),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None or row["disabled"]:
            return False
        expires_at = _parse_time(row["expires_at"])
        last_used = _parse_time(row["last_used_at"]) or now
        return (expires_at is None or expires_at > now) and last_used + self.session_idle > now

    def end_session(self, secret: str) -> None:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM credentials WHERE secret = ? AND kind = ?",
                (secret, CredentialKind.session),
            )

    # Authentication

    def resolve(self, secret: str) -> Caller | None:
        """
        Return the Caller for a credential secret, or `None` if it is not valid
        now. Resolving a Session counts as using it; resolving one of its
        Delegated Tokens does not.
        """
        now = self.clock()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT c.id AS cid, c.kind AS ckind, c.grants, c.expires_at, c.parent_id, "
                + "u.* FROM credentials c JOIN users u ON u.id = c.user_id WHERE c.secret = ?",
                (secret,),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None or row["disabled"]:
                return None
            expires_at = _parse_time(row["expires_at"])
            if expires_at is not None and expires_at <= now:
                return None
            if row["ckind"] in (CredentialKind.session, CredentialKind.delegated):
                session_id = (
                    row["parent_id"] if row["ckind"] == CredentialKind.delegated else row["cid"]
                )
                session = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM credentials WHERE id = ?", (session_id,)
                ).fetchone()
                # A UI calling the API on its own is not the person using the Session.
                used = row["ckind"] == CredentialKind.session
                if session is None or not self._session_alive(conn, session, now, use=used):
                    return None
            user = self._user_from_row(conn, row)
        return self._caller(user, row["cid"], row["ckind"], row["grants"])

    def _caller(
        self, user: User, credential_id: str, credential_kind: str, token_grants: str | None
    ) -> Caller:
        user_grants: list[Grant] = []
        for role in user.roles:
            grants = self.roles.get(role)
            if grants is None:
                logger.warning("User %s has undefined Role %r; it grants nothing", user.id, role)
                continue
            user_grants.extend(grants)
        grant_sets = [tuple(user_grants)]
        if token_grants is not None:
            grant_sets.append(tuple(Grant.parse(g) for g in json.loads(token_grants)))
        return Caller(
            user_id=user.id,
            grant_sets=tuple(grant_sets),
            credential_id=credential_id,
            credential_kind=credential_kind,

def sign_in_person(
    self,
    provider: str,
    subject: str,
    *,
    email: str | None,
    email_verified: bool,
    name: str,
    role_sources: dict[str, list[str]],
) -> User:
    """
    Find or create the User for an Identity Provider's assertion, after the
    caller has decided the person is admitted.

    The User is found by its Linked Identity, else by a verified email
    matching an existing User (linking the identity to it), else created.
    An unverified email is not stored, so it can never take over an account.
    Each entry of `role_sources` replaces that source's Role assignments,
    leaving assignments from other sources (and manual ones) alone.

    Raises `UserDisabled` if the User is disabled.
    """
    verified_email = email.lower() if email and email_verified else None
    with self._connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT u.* FROM linked_identities l JOIN users u ON u.id = l.user_id "
            + "WHERE l.provider = ? AND l.subject = ?",
            (provider, subject),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None and verified_email is not None:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ? AND kind = ?",
                (verified_email, UserKind.person),
            ).fetchone()
        now = self.clock().isoformat()
        if row is None:
            user_id = _new_id("usr")
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO users (id, name, email, kind, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (user_id, name, verified_email, UserKind.person, now),
            )
        else:
            user_id = row["id"]
            if row["disabled"]:
                raise UserDisabled(f"User {user_id} is disabled")
            conn.execute("UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?", (name, user_id))
            if verified_email and row["email"] != verified_email:
                taken = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE email = ?", (verified_email,)
                ).fetchone()
                if not taken:
                    conn.execute(
                        "UPDATE users SET email = ? WHERE id = ?", (verified_email, user_id)
                    )
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO linked_identities (provider, subject, user_id, created_at) "
            + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (provider, subject, user_id, now),
        )
        for source, roles in role_sources.items():
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM role_assignments WHERE user_id = ? AND source = ?",
                (user_id, source),
            )
            for role in roles:
                if role not in self.roles:
                    logger.warning("Sign-in source %s names undefined Role %r", source, role)
                    continue
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO role_assignments (user_id, role, source) "
                    + "VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                    (user_id, role, source),
                )
        user_row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone()
        return self._user_from_row(conn, user_row)

def delegate(self, session_secret: str, ui_name: str, grants: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """
    The Delegated Token for a UI acting on behalf of a Session, created on
    first use. `grants`, the UI's configured Grants, narrows it like a
    narrowed Personal Access Token, and is updated on each call so a config
    change applies at once. Raises `ValueError` unless `session_secret` is
    a live Session.
    """
    grants_json = (
        json.dumps([str(Grant.parse(g)) for g in grants]) if grants is not None else None
    )
    with self._connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM credentials WHERE secret = ? AND kind = ?",
            (session_secret, CredentialKind.session),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None or not self._session_alive(conn, row, self.clock()):
            raise ValueError("Only a live Session can be delegated")
        existing = conn.execute(
            "SELECT secret FROM credentials WHERE parent_id = ? AND kind = ? AND name = ?",
            (row["id"], CredentialKind.delegated, ui_name),
        ).fetchone()
        if existing is not None:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE credentials SET grants = ? WHERE secret = ?",
                (grants_json, existing["secret"]),
            )
            return existing["secret"]
        secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO credentials "
            + "(id, secret, kind, user_id, name, grants, created_at, parent_id) "
            + "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (
                _new_id("dlg"),
                secret,
                CredentialKind.delegated,
                row["user_id"],
                ui_name,
                grants_json,
                self.clock().isoformat(),
                row["id"],
            ),
        )
        return secret

def session_is_live(self, secret: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a Session is still valid, without counting this check as use."""
    now = self.clock()
    with self._connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT c.expires_at, c.last_used_at, u.disabled FROM credentials c "
            + "JOIN users u ON u.id = c.user_id WHERE c.secret = ? AND c.kind = ?",
            (secret, CredentialKind.session),
        ).fetchone()
    if row is None or row["disabled"]:
        return False
    expires_at = _parse_time(row["expires_at"])
    last_used = _parse_time(row["last_used_at"]) or now
    return (expires_at is None or expires_at > now) and last_used + self.session_idle > now

def resolve(self, secret: str) -> Caller | None:
    """
    Return the Caller for a credential secret, or `None` if it is not valid
    now. Resolving a Session counts as using it; resolving one of its
    Delegated Tokens does not.
    """
    now = self.clock()
    with self._connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT c.id AS cid, c.kind AS ckind, c.grants, c.expires_at, c.parent_id, "
            + "u.* FROM credentials c JOIN users u ON u.id = c.user_id WHERE c.secret = ?",
            (secret,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None or row["disabled"]:
            return None
        expires_at = _parse_time(row["expires_at"])
        if expires_at is not None and expires_at <= now:
            return None
        if row["ckind"] in (CredentialKind.session, CredentialKind.delegated):
            session_id = (
                row["parent_id"] if row["ckind"] == CredentialKind.delegated else row["cid"]
            )
            session = conn.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM credentials WHERE id = ?", (session_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            # A UI calling the API on its own is not the person using the Session.
            used = row["ckind"] == CredentialKind.session
            if session is None or not self._session_alive(conn, session, now, use=used):
                return None
        user = self._user_from_row(conn, row)
    return self._caller(user, row["cid"], row["ckind"], row["grants"])

Caddyfile for running woodglue behind Caddy.

Caddyfile for running woodglue behind Caddy (see docs/adr/0004).

wgl caddy config <site> prints a Caddyfile that:

  • serves <site> with Caddy's automatic HTTPS;
  • removes client-sent X-Woodglue-* headers, which only woodglue may set;
  • serves each Static UI's files from disk, after asking woodglue's /auth/verify through forward_auth whether the viewer may open it;
  • sends everything else to woodglue: the API, docs, login, the Console, and Process-backed UIs, whose processes woodglue runs on ports it picks at start and whose Session handling (cookie stripping, Delegated Tokens, closing websockets on logout) stays in one place.

The operator installs it and reloads Caddy. Caddy holds no Users, Sessions, or Grants; woodglue stays the only place that decides who may do what.

def caddyfile(config: WoodglueConfig, site: str) -> str:
    """The Caddyfile for `site`. UI paths in `config` must already be absolute."""
    upstream = woodglue_address(config)
    lines = [
        f"{site} {{",
        "\tencode zstd gzip",
        "",
        "\t# Identity headers come only from woodglue.",
        "\trequest_header -X-Woodglue-User",
        "\trequest_header -X-Woodglue-Token",
    ]
    for name, entry in sorted(config.uis.items()):
        if not entry.is_static:
            continue
        lines += [
            "",
            f"\t# Static UI '{name}': files from disk, access checked by woodglue.",
            f"\tredir /ui/{name} /ui/{name}/ 308",
            f"\thandle /ui/{name}/* {{",
            # `route` keeps this order; Caddy would otherwise strip the prefix
            # before forward_auth, which then reports the wrong path to woodglue.
            "\t\troute {",
        ]
        if not entry.public:
            lines += [
                f"\t\t\tforward_auth {upstream} {{",
                f"\t\t\t\turi /auth/verify?ui={name}",
                "\t\t\t}",
            ]
        lines += [
            f"\t\t\turi strip_prefix /ui/{name}",
            f"\t\t\troot * {entry.path}",
        ]
        if entry.spa_fallback:
            # Like woodglue's own spa_fallback: client routes get index.html, a
            # missing file with an extension stays a 404.
            lines += [
                "\t\t\t@client_route {",
                "\t\t\t\tnot path_regexp \\.[^/]+$",
                "\t\t\t\tnot file",
                "\t\t\t}",
                "\t\t\trewrite @client_route /index.html",
            ]
        lines += [
            "\t\t\tfile_server",
            "\t\t}",
            "\t}",
        ]
    lines += [
        "",
        "\t# The API, docs, login, the Console, and Process-backed UIs.",
        "\thandle {",
        f"\t\treverse_proxy {upstream}",
        "\t}",
        "}",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

docs.text:
wgl login and wgl logout.

wgl login and wgl logout: Personal Access Tokens for remote servers.

login gets a token the way gh auth login does:

  • It listens on a random port on 127.0.0.1 and opens the browser at the server's /auth/cli page (signing in first if needed), passing that loopback address and a PKCE challenge.
  • After the person approves, the server redirects the browser to the loopback address with a one-time code.
  • The CLI exchanges the code and its PKCE verifier for the token at /auth/cli/token, so the token never travels in a URL.

Tokens are stored per server URL in credentials.json under $WOODGLUE_CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.config/woodglue), readable only by you. woodglue.client.WoodglueClient uses a stored token when given no other. logout revokes the token on the server and forgets it.

def login(
    server: str,
    name: str = "wgl",
    open_browser: Callable[[str], None] = _open_in_browser,
    timeout: float = LOGIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
) -> StoredToken:
    """
    Get a Personal Access Token for `server` through the browser and store it.
    Raises `RuntimeError` if the browser does not come back in time or the
    server refuses.
    """
    server = normalize_server(server)
    verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
    state = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    result = _Callback()
    listener = _listener(result)
    port = listener.server_address[1]
    thread = threading.Thread(target=listener.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    try:
        query = urlencode(
            {
                "redirect_uri": f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/callback",
                "state": state,
                "code_challenge": pkce_challenge(verifier),
                "name": name,
            }
        )
        open_browser(f"{server}/auth/cli?{query}")
        if not result.done.wait(timeout):
            raise RuntimeError("Timed out waiting for the browser to approve")
    finally:
        listener.shutdown()
        listener.server_close()
    params = result.params or {}
    if params.get("state") != state or "code" not in params:
        raise RuntimeError("The browser came back without a valid approval")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{server}/auth/cli/token",
        data=json.dumps({"code": params["code"], "code_verifier": verifier}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as resp:
            issued = json.load(resp)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{server} refused the code: HTTP {exc.code}") from exc
    stored = StoredToken(token=issued["token"], token_id=issued["id"])
    credentials = load_credentials()
    credentials[server] = stored
    _save_credentials(credentials)
    return stored

def logout(server: str) -> bool:
    """
    Revoke the stored token for `server` and forget it. Returns whether there
    was one. The token is forgotten even if the server cannot be reached.
    """
    server = normalize_server(server)
    credentials = load_credentials()
    stored = credentials.pop(server, None)
    if stored is None:
        return False
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{server}/rpc",
        data=json.dumps(
            {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "method": "system.revoke_token",
                "params": {"token_id": stored.token_id},
                "id": 1,
            }
        ).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {stored.token}"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30):
            pass
    except OSError:
        pass
    _save_credentials(credentials)
    return True

    return result

@main_at.actions.wrap
def start(ctx: RunContext) -> None:  # pyright: ignore[reportUnusedParameter]
    """Start the server (and optionally the engine)"""
    import tornado.ioloop

    from woodglue.apps.server import create_app

    root: WoodglueMain = ctx.path.get("/")  # pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]
    root.data.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data_dir = root.data.resolve()

    config = load_config(data_dir)
    _resolve_storage(config, data_dir)

    from woodglue.log_setup import setup_logging

    print(f"  {setup_logging(config)}")

    # CLI args override config values
    host = root.host if root.host != "127.0.0.1" else config.host
    port = root.port if root.port != 5321 else config.port

    # Auth setup. Never print the token: under systemd stdout goes to the journal.
    auth_store = None
    if config.auth.enabled:
        from woodglue.auth_store import AuthStore

        assert config.storage.auth_db is not None
        auth_store = AuthStore(config.storage.auth_db, config.auth.resolved_roles())
        auth_store.ensure_admin_token()
        print("  Auth enabled; run 'wgl token' to see the admin token")
    elif host not in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"):
        print(f"  WARNING: auth is disabled and the server listens on {host}; anyone who")
        print("  can reach it has full access")

    namespaces = load_namespaces(config.namespaces, data_dir)

    # Build MountContext for every namespace
    mounts: dict[str, MountContext] = {
        prefix: MountContext(prefix, data_dir) for prefix in namespaces
    }

    # Mount and build engines for namespaces with run_engine=True
    from lythonic.compose.engine import StorageConfig as LythStorageConfig

    from woodglue.engine import EngineRegistry, create_engine

    registry = EngineRegistry()
    for prefix, (ns, entry) in namespaces.items():
        if entry.run_engine:
            mount = mounts[prefix]
            storage = LythStorageConfig()
            storage.resolve_paths(mount.state_dir)
            storage.log_file = None  # global logging already configured
            ns.mount(storage)
            engine = create_engine(mount, ns)
            with mount.activate():
                triggers = engine.trigger_manager.activate_configured()
            registry.register(engine)
            if triggers.activated:
                print(f"  Triggers activated for '{prefix}': {', '.join(triggers.activated)}")
            for name in triggers.left_disabled:
                print(f"  Trigger '{name}' left disabled in '{prefix}'")

    from woodglue.apps.ui_process import UiProcesses

    api_host = "127.0.0.1" if host in ("0.0.0.0", "::", "") else host
    ui_processes = UiProcesses(config.uis, f"http://{api_host}:{port}")

    # Always mount the system namespace (introspection + engine facade)
    from woodglue.apps.system_api import build_system_namespace

    system_ns = build_system_namespace(
        namespaces,
        registry if registry.has_engines() else None,
        auth_store,
        uis=config.uis,
        console=config.ui.enabled,
        ui_processes=ui_processes,
    )
    system_entry = NamespaceEntry(gref="builtin:system", expose_api=True)
    namespaces["system"] = (system_ns, system_entry)
    mounts["system"] = MountContext("system", data_dir)

    app = create_app(
        namespaces=namespaces,
        config=config,
        engine_registry=registry,
        mounts=mounts,
        auth_store=auth_store,
        ui_processes=ui_processes,
    )
    server = app.listen(port, host)
    print(f"Woodglue listening on http://{host}:{port}")
    print(f"  RPC endpoint: http://{host}:{port}/rpc")
    if config.docs.enabled:
        print(f"  LLM docs:     http://{host}:{port}/docs/llms.txt")
    if config.ui.enabled:
        print(f"  Console:      http://{host}:{port}/console/")
    for name in config.uis:
        print(f"  UI:           http://{host}:{port}/ui/{name}/")

    if registry.has_engines():
        print(f"  Engine: enabled ({', '.join(registry.list_prefixes())})")

    ioloop = tornado.ioloop.IOLoop.current()

    # Shut down on the running loop so engine tasks are cancelled by live loop code,
    # rather than via run_until_complete after the loop has already stopped.
    async def _shutdown(signal_name: str) -> None:
        print(f"Received {signal_name}, shutting down")
        server.stop()
        await registry.stop_all()
        await ui_processes.stop_all()
        ioloop.stop()

    _install_shutdown_handlers(
        ioloop.asyncio_loop,  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
        lambda signal_name: ioloop.add_callback(_shutdown, signal_name),
    )

    pid_path = _pid_file(data_dir)
    pid_path.write_text(str(os.getpid()))

    # Start trigger managers, then UI processes, once the IOLoop is running
    if registry.has_engines():
        ioloop.add_callback(registry.start_all)
    if ui_processes.has_processes():
        ioloop.add_callback(ui_processes.start_all)

    try:
        ioloop.start()
    finally:
        pid_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

@main_at.actions.wrap
def run(ctx: RunContext, nsref: str) -> None:  # pyright: ignore[reportUnusedParameter]
    """Run a callable or DAG once"""
    import asyncio
    import inspect
    import json

    root: WoodglueMain = ctx.path.get("/")  # pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]
    data_dir = root.data.resolve()
    config = load_config(data_dir)
    _resolve_storage(config, data_dir)
    namespaces = load_namespaces(config.namespaces, data_dir)

    node = None
    node_prefix = ""
    for prefix, (ns, _entry) in namespaces.items():
        try:
            node = ns.get(nsref)
            node_prefix = prefix
            break
        except KeyError:
            continue

    if node is None:
        print(f"'{nsref}' not found in any namespace")
        return

    async def _run() -> None:
        result = node()
        if inspect.isawaitable(result):
            result = await result
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str))

    import getpass

    from lythonic.compose.dag_provenance import initiated_by

    # asyncio.run copies the current context, so the node sees the mount and initiator
    with MountContext(node_prefix, data_dir).activate(), initiated_by(f"cli:{getpass.getuser()}"):
        asyncio.run(_run())

class WoodglueClient:
    """
    Async client for woodglue JSON-RPC servers.

    Optionally loads the OpenAPI spec to auto-resolve return types from
    `x-global-ref` vendor extensions.

    Resolution priority on `call()`:
    1. Explicit `return_type` parameter
    2. `resolver` callable (receives the `x-global-ref` string)
    3. Type from `load_spec()` if loaded
    4. Return raw dict/primitive
    """

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, *, token: str | None = None, data_dir: Path | None = None):
        self._base_url: str = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._http: AsyncHTTPClient = AsyncHTTPClient()
        self._request_id: int = 0
        self._return_types: dict[str, type[BaseModel]] = {}
        self._return_grefs: dict[str, str] = {}
        if token is not None:
            self._token: str | None = token
        elif data_dir is not None:
            self._token = _local_admin_token(data_dir / "auth.db")
        else:
            from woodglue.cli_login import stored_token

            self._token = stored_token(base_url)

    async def load_spec(self, strict: bool = False) -> None:
        """
        Fetch `/docs/openapi.json` and resolve `x-global-ref` types.

        With `strict=True`, raises `ImportError` if any gref cannot be
        resolved. With `strict=False`, skips unresolvable grefs.
        """
        from lythonic import GlobalRef

        headers: dict[str, str] = {}
        if self._token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self._token}"
        resp = await self._http.fetch(f"{self._base_url}/docs/openapi.json", headers=headers)
        spec = json.loads(resp.body)

        for _path, path_item in spec.get("paths", {}).items():
            for _http_method, operation in path_item.items():
                op_id = operation.get("operationId")
                if not op_id:
                    continue

                resp_content = (
                    operation.get("responses", {})
                    .get("200", {})
                    .get("content", {})
                    .get("application/json", {})
                )
                schema = resp_content.get("schema", {})
                gref_str = schema.get("x-global-ref")
                if not gref_str:
                    continue

                self._return_grefs[op_id] = gref_str

                try:
                    gref = GlobalRef(gref_str)
                    cls = gref.get_instance()
                    if isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, BaseModel):
                        self._return_types[op_id] = cls
                except Exception as exc:
                    if strict:
                        raise ImportError(
                            f"Cannot resolve x-global-ref '{gref_str}' for method '{op_id}'"
                        ) from exc

    async def call(
        self,
        method: str,
        *,
        return_type: type[BaseModel] | None = None,
        resolver: Callable[[str], type[BaseModel] | None] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Any:
        """
        Call a JSON-RPC method and return the deserialized result.

        `kwargs` are sent as the JSON-RPC `params` object. BaseModel
        values in kwargs are serialized via `model_dump(mode="json")`.
        """
        self._request_id += 1

        params: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            if isinstance(value, BaseModel):
                params[key] = value.model_dump(mode="json")
            else:
                params[key] = value

        body = json.dumps(
            {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "method": method,
                "params": params,
                "id": self._request_id,
            }
        )

        headers: dict[str, str] = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if self._token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self._token}"

        req = HTTPRequest(
            f"{self._base_url}/rpc",
            method="POST",
            body=body,
            headers=headers,
        )
        resp = await self._http.fetch(req)
        data = json.loads(resp.body)

        if "error" in data:
            err = data["error"]
            raise WoodglueRpcError(err["code"], err["message"], err.get("data"))

        result = data.get("result")

        resolved_type = return_type
        if resolved_type is None and resolver is not None:
            gref_str = self._return_grefs.get(method)
            if gref_str:
                resolved_type = resolver(gref_str)
        if resolved_type is None:
            resolved_type = self._return_types.get(method)

        if resolved_type is not None and isinstance(result, dict):
            return resolved_type.model_validate(result)
        return result

  • path: a Static UI, a directory of built files (relative to the data dir), such as a single-page app built with base: "/ui/<name>/". With spa_fallback, paths without a file extension that match no file return index.html, so client-side routes survive a reload; a missing .js file is still a 404.

  • upstream: the URL of a server run elsewhere, proxied to as is. It must serve under /ui/<name> too.

A Process-backed UI (all but path) gets the viewing User's identity in request headers (see woodglue.ui_support), including a Delegated Token to call the API as them. grants limits that token to the overlap of the viewer's Grants and these, e.g. ["call reports", "read reports"], so a compromised UI process cannot use everything an admin viewer may. class UiEntry(BaseModel):
    """
    A project UI served at `/ui/<name>/`, next to the Console. Exactly one of
    these says what it is:

    - `path`: a Static UI, a directory of built files (relative to the data
      dir), such as a single-page app built with `base: "/ui/<name>/"`. With
      `spa_fallback`, paths without a file extension that match no file return
      `index.html`, so client-side routes survive a reload; a missing `.js`
      file is still a 404.
    - `kind: streamlit` with `app`: a Streamlit script that woodglue runs and
      proxies to (see `woodglue.apps.ui_process`).
    - `command`: any other server that woodglue runs and proxies to. Its
      arguments may use `{port}` (a free loopback port woodglue picks) and
      `{base_path}` (`/ui/<name>`); the server must listen on that port and
      serve under that path.
    - `upstream`: the URL of a server run elsewhere, proxied to as is. It must
      serve under `/ui/<name>` too.

    A Process-backed UI (all but `path`) gets the viewing User's identity in
    request headers (see `woodglue.ui_support`), including a Delegated Token to
    call the API as them. `grants` limits that token to the overlap of the
    viewer's Grants and these, e.g. `["call reports", "read reports"]`, so a
    compromised UI process cannot use everything an admin viewer may. Without
    `grants` the token carries all of the viewer's Grants. `ready_path` is what
    woodglue polls until the process answers; `dev` turns on the framework's
    reload.

    Opening any UI needs `view` on `ui:<name>` unless `public`.
    """

    path: str | None = None
    kind: UiKind | None = None
    app: str | None = None
    command: list[str] | None = None
    upstream: str | None = None
    cwd: str | None = None
    env: dict[str, str] = {}
    ready_path: str | None = None
    dev: bool = False
    grants: list[str] | None = None
    label: str | None = None
    spa_fallback: bool = True
    public: bool = False

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _one_source(self) -> UiEntry:
        sources = [self.path, self.kind, self.command, self.upstream]
        if sum(s is not None for s in sources) != 1:
            raise ValueError("A UI needs exactly one of path, kind, command, or upstream")
        if self.kind == UiKind.streamlit and not self.app:
            raise ValueError("kind: streamlit needs app, the path of the Streamlit script")
        if self.grants is not None:
            if self.is_static:
                raise ValueError(
                    "grants apply to Process-backed UIs; a Static UI runs in the browser "
                    + "with the viewer's Session"
                )
            for grant in self.grants:
                Grant.parse(grant)
        return self

    @property
    def is_static(self) -> bool:
        return self.path is not None

    @property
    def is_supervised(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind is not None or self.command is not None
