class ProviderConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    One Identity Provider in `auth.providers`.

    - `kind: oidc` covers Google, Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, and other OpenID
      Connect providers; `issuer` is the URL its discovery document hangs off.
    - `kind: github` uses GitHub's OAuth2; `github_url` and `github_api_url`
      point at GitHub Enterprise when needed.
    - `kind: trusted_proxy_jwt` trusts a reverse proxy that signs each request's
      identity as a JWT in `header`, e.g. Cloudflare Access
      (`Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`), Google IAP (`x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion`), or
      oauth2-proxy. The JWT is checked against `jwks_url`, `issuer`, and
      `audience`; `email_claim` and `groups_claim` name the claims to read.
    - `kind: trusted_proxy_header` trusts a plain `header` such as
      `X-Forwarded-Email`, with optional `name_header` and `groups_header`
      (comma-separated), but only from `trusted_sources` (IPs or CIDRs).
      Anyone who reaches woodglue without the proxy can forge the header, so
      `trusted_sources` is required.

    With a trusted proxy there is no login page: the first request carrying a
    valid assertion signs the person in and starts a Session.

    `client_secret` (and any other string) may reference environment variables
    as `${NAME}`. `default_roles` and the Roles that `group_roles` maps a
    person's groups to are re-applied at every login, so removing someone from
    a group takes their Role away at their next login.
    """

    id: str = Field(pattern=r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$")
    kind: ProviderKind
    label: str | None = None
    issuer: str | None = None
    client_id: str | None = None
    client_secret: str | None = None
    scopes: list[str] | None = None
    groups_claim: str = "groups"
    email_claim: str = "email"
    header: str | None = None
    jwks_url: str | None = None
    audience: str | None = None
    name_header: str | None = None
    groups_header: str | None = None
    trusted_sources: list[str] = []
    trust_email: bool = False
    """
    Treat the `email` claim as verified even without `email_verified: true`.
    Only for providers whose addresses the organization controls, such as a
    single-tenant Entra ID, which does not send `email_verified`.
    """
    github_url: str = "https://github.com"
    github_api_url: str = "https://api.github.com"
    admit: AdmitRules
    default_roles: list[str] = []
    group_roles: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

    @field_validator("client_id", "client_secret", "issuer", "audience")
    @classmethod
    def _expand_env(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        return expand_env(value, os.environ) if value is not None else None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> ProviderConfig:
        required: dict[ProviderKind, list[str]] = {
            ProviderKind.oidc: ["issuer", "client_id", "client_secret"],
            ProviderKind.github: ["client_id", "client_secret"],
            ProviderKind.trusted_proxy_jwt: ["header", "jwks_url", "issuer", "audience"],
            ProviderKind.trusted_proxy_header: ["header", "trusted_sources"],
        }
        missing = [f for f in required[self.kind] if not getattr(self, f)]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"Provider '{self.id}': kind {self.kind} needs {', '.join(missing)}")
        for source in self.trusted_sources:
            ipaddress.ip_network(source, strict=False)
        if self.admit.is_empty():
            raise ValueError(
                f"Provider '{self.id}': admit needs at least one rule "
                + "(email_domains, emails, groups, or anyone: true)"
            )
        return self

    @property
    def display_name(self) -> str:
        return self.label or self.id.capitalize()

    def requested_scopes(self) -> list[str]:
        if self.scopes is not None:
            return self.scopes
        if self.kind == ProviderKind.github:
            return ["read:user", "user:email", "read:org"]
        return ["openid", "email", "profile"]

class AuthConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    Authentication and authorization settings.

    `roles` maps a Role name to its Grants, written as `"<action> <pattern>"`
    strings (see `woodglue.access`). The `admin` Role is built in. When
    `enabled` is false, every request runs as an anonymous Caller with all
    Grants.

    `providers` lists the Identity Providers people can sign in with (see
    `ProviderConfig`); with none, the login page takes a Personal Access Token.
    People whose verified email is in `admins` get the `admin` Role at login.
    `public_url` is the server's address as browsers see it (e.g.
    `https://wg.example.com`), used to build login callback URLs when woodglue
    runs behind a proxy; by default it is taken from each request.
    """

    enabled: bool = True
    roles: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    providers: list[ProviderConfig] = []
    admins: list[str] = []
    public_url: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> AuthConfig:
        defined = resolve_roles(self.roles)
        ids = [p.id for p in self.providers]
        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
            raise ValueError("auth.providers ids must be unique")
        for provider in self.providers:
            named = set(provider.default_roles)
            for roles in provider.group_roles.values():
                named.update(roles)
            unknown = sorted(named - set(defined))
            if unknown:
                raise ValueError(f"Provider '{provider.id}' names undefined Roles: {unknown}")
        return self

    def resolved_roles(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Grant, ...]]:
        return resolve_roles(self.roles)

    def provider(self, provider_id: str) -> ProviderConfig | None:
        return next((p for p in self.providers if p.id == provider_id), None)

def expand_env(text: str, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
    """
    Replace `${NAME}` references with values from `env`, so secrets stay out of
    `woodglue.yaml`. A missing variable is an error rather than an empty string.

    >>> expand_env("${ID}-x", {"ID": "abc"})
    'abc-x'
    >>> expand_env("${NOPE}", {})
    Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
    ValueError: Environment variable NOPE is not set
    """

    def replace(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        name = match.group(1)
        if name not in env:
            raise ValueError(f"Environment variable {name} is not set")
        return env[name]

    return _ENV_REF.sub(replace, text)

docs.title: woodglue.log_setup
docs.text:
Logging setup for wgl start: journal, rotated file, or a logging: dictConfig.

Logging setup for wgl start.

Woodglue configures the root logger itself from woodglue.yaml; lythonic only contributes NodeRunLogFilter, which adds run_id and node_label to records logged inside a node run.

docs.title: Default behavior
docs.text:
Under systemd (detected by JOURNAL_STREAM in the environment), records go to stderr without a timestamp, since the journal adds its own. Every line carries an sd-daemon priority prefix (<7> DEBUG, <6> INFO, <4> WARNING, <3> ERROR, <2> CRITICAL) so journald records the right priority. No file log is written unless storage.log_file is set explicitly.

Outside systemd, records go to <data>/wgl.log (or storage.log_file).

Every file log is a RotatingFileHandler, rotated at storage.log_max_bytes (default 10 MB) keeping storage.log_backup_count backups (default 5).

storage:
  log_file: logs/wgl.log   # relative to the data dir; null disables the file log
  log_level: INFO          # root level, INFO when unset
  log_max_bytes: 10485760
  log_backup_count: 5
  loggers:                 # per-logger levels
    tornado.access: WARNING

With log_file: null outside systemd, records go to stderr with a timestamp so they are not lost. An unknown level name in log_level or loggers stops wgl start with a ValueError rather than silently falling back to DEBUG.

docs.title: Custom setup with logging:
docs.text:
A top-level logging: section in woodglue.yaml is passed to logging.config.dictConfig and replaces everything above, including the storage.log_* settings. Attach NodeRunLogFilter to keep the run context:

logging:
  version: 1
  disable_existing_loggers: false
  filters:
    noderun:
      (): lythonic.compose.log_context.NodeRunLogFilter
  formatters:
    plain:
      format: "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(name)s] run=%(run_id)s %(message)s"
  handlers:
    console:
      class: logging.StreamHandler
      formatter: plain
      filters: [noderun]
  root:
    level: INFO
    handlers: [console]

Keep disable_existing_loggers: false: the dictConfig default of true silences every logger created before setup, including woodglue's own.

class JournalFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    """
    Prefix every output line with the sd-daemon priority of the record's level.

    journald reads the prefix per line, so the continuation lines of a traceback
    keep the record's priority instead of defaulting to INFO.
    """

    @override
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        prefix = f"<{_sd_priority(record.levelno)}>"
        return "\n".join(prefix + line for line in super().format(record).split("\n"))

def setup_logging(config: WoodglueConfig, env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """
    Configure the root logger for `wgl start` and return a one-line description
    of what is in effect, e.g. `Logging to journal`.

    Expects `config.storage` already resolved against the data dir. Safe to call
    repeatedly: handlers from a previous call are replaced, not duplicated.
    `env` defaults to `os.environ`.
    """
    env = os.environ if env is None else env
    root = logging.getLogger()
    _remove_installed_handlers(root)

    if config.logging is not None:
        logging.config.dictConfig(config.logging)
        return "Logging per woodglue.yaml logging: section"

    storage = config.storage
    under_systemd = "JOURNAL_STREAM" in env
    log_file: Path | None = storage.log_file
    if under_systemd and not storage.log_file_explicit:
        log_file = None

    targets: list[str] = []
    if under_systemd:
        _add_handler(
            root, "journal", logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr), JournalFormatter(_RECORD_FORMAT)
        )
        targets.append("journal")
    if log_file is not None:
        log_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file_handler = logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler(
            log_file,
            maxBytes=storage.log_max_bytes,
            backupCount=storage.log_backup_count,
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        _add_handler(root, "file", file_handler, logging.Formatter(_TIMESTAMPED_FORMAT))
        targets.append(str(log_file))
    if not targets:
        _add_handler(
            root,
            "stderr",
            logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr),
            logging.Formatter(_TIMESTAMPED_FORMAT),
        )
        targets.append("stderr")

    root.setLevel(storage.log_level.upper())
    for logger_name, level_name in storage.loggers.items():
        logging.getLogger(logger_name).setLevel(level_name.upper())

    return "Logging to " + " and ".join(targets)

docs.title: woodglue.ui_support
docs.text:
Helpers for code running inside a Process-backed UI.

Helpers for code running inside a Process-backed UI, such as a Streamlit app.

woodglue's proxy adds two headers to every request it forwards (see woodglue.apps.ui_proxy):

  • X-Woodglue-User: JSON describing the viewing User.
  • X-Woodglue-Token: a Delegated Token for that User's Session, present when they signed in through the browser.

and starts the process with WOODGLUE_URL, the API's loopback address. current_client combines them into a woodglue.client.WoodglueClient that calls the API as the viewer, with exactly their Grants:

import asyncio

import streamlit as st
from woodglue.ui_support import current_client, current_user

me = current_user()
st.write(f"Hello, {me.name if me else 'stranger'}")


async def load_totals():
    return await current_client().call("reports.daily_totals", day="2026-10-01")


st.write(asyncio.run(load_totals()))

Streamlit runs the script without an event loop, so make the client inside the coroutine that asyncio.run drives, as above.

Without headers, both read Streamlit's st.context.headers; other frameworks pass their request headers. The headers are only trustworthy behind woodglue, which strips client-sent copies, so the UI process must listen on loopback only, as it does when woodglue runs it.

def current_user(headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> ViewingUser | None:
    """
    The User viewing the UI, or `None` if the request did not come through
    woodglue.

    >>> current_user({"x-woodglue-user": '{"id": "u1", "name": "Ann", "roles": ["viewer"]}'})
    ViewingUser(id='u1', name='Ann', email=None, roles=('viewer',))
    >>> current_user({}) is None
    True
    """
    raw = _header(headers if headers is not None else _streamlit_headers(), USER_HEADER)
    if raw is None:
        return None
    data = json.loads(raw)
    return ViewingUser(
        id=data.get("id"),
        name=data.get("name", ""),
        email=data.get("email"),
        roles=tuple(data.get("roles", ())),
    )

docs.text:
A client calling the woodglue API as the viewing User. base_url defaults to WOODGLUE_URL. Without a Delegated Token (e.g. auth is disabled), the client sends no credential.

Source code in src/woodglue/ui_support.py 
def current_client(
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, base_url: str | None = None
) -> WoodglueClient:
    """
    A client calling the woodglue API as the viewing User. `base_url` defaults
    to `WOODGLUE_URL`. Without a Delegated Token (e.g. auth is disabled), the
    client sends no credential.
    """
    url = base_url or os.environ.get("WOODGLUE_URL")
    if not url:
        raise RuntimeError("WOODGLUE_URL is not set; is this process running under woodglue?")
    token = _header(headers if headers is not None else _streamlit_headers(), TOKEN_HEADER)
    return WoodglueClient(url, token=token)

docs.text:
• Users, Roles, and Grants (woodglue.auth_store, woodglue.access): auth.db holds Users, Role assignments, and Personal Access Tokens, and every request is authorized against Grants defined as Roles in woodglue.yaml. Discovery (list_namespaces, list_methods, describe_method, llms.txt, method docs, openapi.json) shows only what the Caller may see. New system methods: whoami, create_token, list_tokens, revoke_token, and admin-only User management. New CLI: wgl user. Existing tokens migrate to the built-in admin Service User, and wgl token keeps working.
  • Sign-in with Identity Providers: auth.providers with kind: oidc (Google, Entra ID, Auth0, Okta) or kind: github. woodglue is its own OAuth client (PKCE, state, nonce). Each provider needs admit rules (email_domains, emails, groups, or anyone: true); default_roles, group_roles, and auth.admins are re-synced at every sign-in. A second provider with the same verified email links to the same User.
  • Trusted-proxy Identity Providers: kind: trusted_proxy_jwt (Cloudflare Access, Google IAP, oauth2-proxy; checked against jwks_url, issuer, audience, expiry) and kind: trusted_proxy_header (honored only from trusted_sources).
  • Sessions: browsers hold an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax Session cookie (12h idle, 7 days at most), set by /auth/login, ended by /auth/logout. The cookie is Secure when auth.public_url is https.
  • Static UIs at /ui/<name>/ via uis.<name> in woodglue.yaml, with spa_fallback, public, and ui.default to choose what / opens. Opening a UI needs view on ui:<name>.
  • Process-backed UIs (Streamlit or any web server) via a Tornado proxy at /ui/<name>/: woodglue supervises the process on a loopback port, relays HTTP and websockets, strips its own Session cookie, and passes X-Woodglue-User and a Delegated Token. uis.<name>.grants narrows that token. App code uses woodglue.ui_support.current_user / current_client. Example in examples/streamlit/.
  • Caddy as an optional edge: GET /auth/verify answers Caddy's forward_auth, and wgl caddy config <site> prints a Caddyfile that serves Static UIs from disk and proxies everything else to woodglue.
  • wgl login --server=URL gets a Personal Access Token for a remote server through a loopback redirect with PKCE, storing it in $WOODGLUE_CONFIG_DIR/credentials.json (mode 0600). WoodglueClient uses the stored token when given none. wgl logout revokes and forgets it.
  • Run attribution: DAG runs record initiated_by (the User for RPC calls, cli:<os user> for wgl run, scheduler for scheduled runs), and trigger changes record changed_by. system.describe_initiators resolves User ids; the Console shows who started each run.
